list_dashboards.name: list_dashboards
list_dashboards.description:
Enumerate Tableau Next dashboards (metadata only) for discovery and
selection in the current org / sandbox.

**Inputs:** `limit`, `offset`, and `minorVersion`. There is NO `label`,
`searchTerm`, or workspace filter -- the tool returns every dashboard the
caller can see across the org, mixing all workspaces.

To list dashboards scoped to a single workspace, use `list_workspace_assets`
(the workspace-scoped listing tool). To filter by label or name, use
`browse_data_assets` with `AssetType=AnalyticsDashboard` (subject to
`browse_data_assets`'s empty-searchTerm caveat), or retrieve the full list
and filter client-side.

**Returns:** `items[]` with id, name / label, owning workspace
(id / name), `lastModifiedDate`, `url`.

**Use when:** you need dashboard identifiers or to browse dashboards.
To actually see one, use `show_dashboard` (renders inline); to inspect
one dashboard's metadata programmatically, use `get_dashboard`.

**Caveats:**

- **`limit:0` returns an empty array** -- treat as a broken boundary,
  NOT as "no results."

- **Scope:** current org only; does NOT copy from another org
  (Prod -> PO).

**Typical flows:**
- Render one for the user: `list_dashboards` -> `show_dashboard`.
- Prepare an update: `list_dashboards` -> `get_dashboard` ->
  `update_dashboard`.

get_dashboard.name: get_dashboard
get_dashboard.description:
**Metadata-only fetch.** If the user wants to *see, open, view, display,
render, bring up, pull up, load, or look at* a dashboard, use
`show_dashboard` instead -- this tool does NOT render.

Retrieve a single dashboard's flat metadata (layout, widgets, owning
workspace, url) without any of its referenced assets (semantic models,
visualizations). Cheap; use when you only need to inspect fields
programmatically.

**Inputs:**
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (path) -- the id or apiName from
  `list_dashboards` or `browse_data_assets`.
- `minorVersion` (optional) -- the Salesforce API minor version
  (e.g. `67.42`), NOT a dashboard revision. Invalid values produce
  `Invalid version` errors.

**Returns:** flat dashboard metadata as a JSON object. Read fields
directly: `response.label`, `response.widgets`, `response.layout`,
`response.folder`, etc. This read tool is NOT double-wrapped (distinct
from `create_dashboard` and `delete_dashboard`, which ARE wrapped).

The response includes a `url` field: this is a canonical external link
to the dashboard in the Analytics app. It does NOT render the dashboard
inline in this conversation -- for inline rendering, call
`show_dashboard`.

**Use when:**
- You need to read specific fields (`label`, `widgets`, `layout`,
  owning workspace) programmatically -- e.g. to inspect a widget's
  configuration, diff two dashboards, or answer a metadata question
  without showing the dashboard to the user.
- You are preparing a follow-up `update_dashboard` call and need the
  current metadata to base edits on.

**Do NOT use when:** the user's intent is to *see* the dashboard --
asks to show, open, view, display, render, bring up, pull up, load,
or look at it, or names/ids a dashboard and wants to see it (its
charts, filters, or layout). Use `show_dashboard` for that -- it
returns the same dashboard bundled with its referenced assets and
renders it inline.

**Scope:** current org only.

show_dashboard.name: show_dashboard
show_dashboard.description:
**Render a dashboard inline for the user.** This is the tool to pick
whenever the user's intent involves *seeing, opening, viewing,
displaying, rendering, bringing up, pulling up, loading, or looking at*
a dashboard. If you only need to read a metadata field programmatically
(no rendering), use `get_dashboard` instead.

**Use when:** the user expresses any intent to *see* a dashboard -- e.g.
asks to **show, open, view, display, render, bring up, pull up, load, or
look at** a dashboard, or names/ids a dashboard and wants to see it (its
charts, filters, or layout). This is the primary tool for putting a
dashboard in front of the user.

**Do NOT use when:**
- You only need to read a specific field (`label`, `widgets`,
  `layout`, owning workspace) programmatically, without showing the
  dashboard to the user.
- You are chaining into `update_dashboard` and just need current
  metadata to base edits on.

Use `get_dashboard` for those -- it is cheaper (no bundled assets) and
does not render.

**What it does:** retrieves the dashboard's full metadata **bundled
together with its referenced assets** (semantic models and
visualizations) in a single response, so the dashboard and its
visualization / filter / parameter widgets can render immediately
without additional per-asset fetches.

**Inputs:**
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (path) -- the id or apiName from `list_dashboards`
  or `browse_data_assets`.
- `addVisualization` -- include referenced visualizations so visualization
  tiles can render. **Always send `true`** (required, single-value).
- `addSdm` -- include referenced semantic models so filter / parameter
  widgets that depend on semantic model metadata can render. **Always send
  `true`** (required, single-value).
- `minorVersion` -- the Salesforce API minor version. **Always send `-1`**
  (latest supported minor version; required, single-value). NOT a dashboard
  revision.
- `pageName` (optional) -- a specific page GUID to load.
- `customViewId` (optional) -- a custom view to load as part of the bundle.
- `height` (optional) -- viewport height in pixels; when passed, only assets
  visible within that height are included.

**Returns:** a bundle object with `dashboard` (the full dashboard metadata:
layout, widgets, owning workspace, url) and `bundledAssets` (a map of asset
id to the referenced semantic model / visualization). Read the dashboard at
`response.dashboard` and its assets at `response.bundledAssets`.

**Scope:** current org only.

dashboardIdOrApiName.description: The id or API name of the dashboard.

addVisualization.description:
Add referenced visualizations to the bundle so visualization
tiles can render. Always send `true` -- the single-value enum
forces this so the returned dashboard is fully renderable.

addSdm.description:
Add referenced semantic models to the bundle so filter /
parameter widgets that depend on semantic model metadata can
render without an extra fetch. Always send `true` -- the
single-value enum forces this.

pageName.description: Specific page name (GUID) of the dashboard.

debug.description: Parameter which is used to return API extra execution details.

forceReload.description: Parameter which is used to indicate if bundle response use cached data or force reload.

minorVersion.description:
Minor supported for the API. Always send `-1` (latest supported
minor version) -- the single-value enum forces this. NOT a
dashboard revision.

customViewId.description: Custom view id (if passed) to load as part of bundle.

height.description: Dashboard height on the viewport in pixels. If passed, bundle only includes assets that display in the height.

render_metric.name: render_metric
render_metric.description:
Render a semantic metric card. Use to visually display a single metric with
its current value, trend, forecast, and insights. Provide the metric's
apiName and the semantic model's apiName; the tool returns a fully-primed
insight bundle envelope (sdm + bundle + submetric + resolved timeRange +
filters + layout) rendered by the metric-standalone MCP renderer. The
renderer's first paint requires zero additional client round-trips.

metricApiName.description: API name of the semantic metric to render.

modelApiName.description: API name of the semantic model (SDM) that owns the metric.

bundleType.description: Insight bundle type. Defaults to BASIC.

layout.description: Renderer layout hint. Defaults to ROW.

create_dashboard.name: create_dashboard
create_dashboard.description:
Create a new Tableau Next dashboard in the current org.

**Body inputs:**
- `name` (REQUIRED) -- developer / API identifier; alphanumeric +
  underscore, NO spaces, e.g. `ReturnAnalyticsDashboard`.
- `label` (REQUIRED) -- display name, free text.
- `workspaceIdOrApiName` (REQUIRED) -- id like `1Dyxx...` or apiName
  from `list_workspaces`. NOT the workspace label with spaces -- that
  404s.
- `description` (optional)
- Optional bulk-create fields: `widgets` (map; pass `{}` if empty),
  `layouts` (array; pass `[]` if empty), `style`, `customConfig`,
  `templateSource`, `backgroundSource`. When you DO pass a non-empty
  `layouts`, each layout MUST carry a full `style` block and a
  `columnCount` (see the write-shape rules below) -- otherwise the
  dashboard renders unstyled.

**Do NOT use the empty-create pattern.** Calling with just
`{name, label, workspaceIdOrApiName}` currently leaks a raw Java NPE:

```
Cannot invoke "java.util.Map.values()" because the return value of
"...getWidgets()" is null
```

At minimum, pass `widgets: {}` AND `layouts: []` -- both are de-facto
required even when empty.

**Recommended pattern -- minimal-create then `update_dashboard`:**

1. `create_dashboard` with
   `{name, label, workspaceIdOrApiName, widgets: {}, layouts: []}`.
2. One of `create_timeseries_viz` / `create_comparative_viz` /
   `create_compositional_viz` / `create_relationship_viz` for each viz.
3. `update_dashboard` to attach widgets and layouts.

This gives you one validated PATCH body to debug instead of a half-good
dashboard if any widget body is malformed.

If you do bulk-create with `widgets` + `layouts` here, the same
write-shape rules from `update_dashboard` apply -- see that tool for
the full rule set. Summary:

- `widget.type` must be LOWERCASE (`"visualization"` or `"text"`).
- Strip `widget.source.label` and `widget.source.type`.
- `layouts[].style` is LOAD-BEARING for rendering and is REQUIRED on
  every layout -- omitting it produces an unstyled dashboard. ALWAYS
  include a full style block. If you have no specific styling, copy the
  canonical defaults verbatim:

  ```json
  "style": {
    "backgroundColor": "#ffffff",
    "gutterColor": "#f3f3f3",
    "cellSpacingX": 4,
    "cellSpacingY": 4
  }
  ```
- 0-based grid coords with modern defaults `columnCount: 48`,
  `rowHeight: 20`, `maxWidth: 1200`. `columnCount` is also required on
  every layout.
- Every `widgets` map key must equal that widget's inner `name` AND
  appear in some `layouts[].pages[].widgets[].name`. Orphans silently
  corrupt rendering.
- **Always name AND label every page.** Each `layouts[].pages[]` entry
  accepts `name` (API id, e.g. `page_1`) and `label` (display name).
  Unlike `add_dashboard_page`, bulk-create here does NOT auto-derive
  `page_N` -- an omitted `name` is stored empty, so any navigation
  widget targeting that page by `page_N` will not resolve, and an
  omitted `label` renders a blank page tab. Set BOTH on the first page
  (and every page) at create time: `name` as the contiguous `page_1`,
  `page_2`, ... sequence, and `label` as a meaningful title from the
  dashboard's purpose (e.g. `"Overview"`), never a bare `"Page 1"`
  placeholder. Do NOT create the dashboard then call
  `add_dashboard_page` just to name page one.

**Returns:** full dashboard metadata including `id`, `name`, `label`,
`url`, `workspaceIdOrApiName`, `widgets` map, `layouts`.

**Typical flow:** `list_workspaces` -> `create_dashboard`
(`{name, label, workspaceIdOrApiName, widgets:{}, layouts:[]}`) ->
`create_*_viz` -> `update_dashboard`.

**Caveats:**

- **Silent name transforms.** No warning is returned -- the response
  simply shows the rewritten `name`. Always read `name` back and verify
  it matches what you sent.
  - Duplicate `name` in the same org -> auto-renamed with a numeric
    suffix.
  - Non-ASCII / unicode characters -> silently stripped.
  - `name` longer than the max length -> silently truncated (observed
    cap around 78 to 80 characters).
  - Spaces in `name` -> silently converted to underscores (despite the
    "NO spaces" rule above, no error is raised).

- **Side effect: workspace cascade.** The new dashboard is auto-added
  to its workspace with `assetUsageType=Created`. Combined with the
  cascade behavior in `delete_workspace`, deleting the workspace WILL
  delete every dashboard authored in it. List workspace assets before
  deleting.

- **Scope:** creates in current org only -- does NOT copy from another
  org.

- **Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
  `{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}`.
  Parse `JSON.parse(response.defaultExc)` to get the body. Note:
  `update_dashboard` does NOT double-wrap; the wrapping is per-tool.

minorVersion.description:
Minor version supported for the API. Always send `-1` (latest
supported minor version) -- the single-value enum forces this
so a compliant client always emits it and can only pick the
one allowed value. NOT a dashboard revision. See
showDashboard.yaml for the same pattern rationale.

name.description:
Developer / API identifier. Alphanumeric + underscore,
NO spaces. Silent rename rules apply (duplicates get a
numeric suffix; spaces become underscores).

workspaceIdOrApiName.description:
Workspace id (`1Dyxx...`) or apiName from
`list_workspaces`. NOT the workspace label with spaces --
that 404s.

widgets.description:
Map of widgetName -> widget definition. Pass `{}` if
empty (server NPEs on null). Each entry is an object:
`{ "type": "<lowercase widget type>", "name":
"<unique widget key>", "source": { "id": "<viz id>",
"name": "<viz apiName>" } }`. Each key in this map
must equal that widget's inner `name` AND appear in
some `layouts[].pages[].widgets[].name`. Orphans
silently corrupt rendering. `widget.type` is
LOWERCASE on write -- one of "visualization", "text",
"filter", "image", "metric", "button", "container",
"extension", "summary", "parameter". Strip
`widget.source.label` and `widget.source.type` if
you copied them from `list_visualizations` -- only
`id` and `name` belong there.

layouts.description:
Pass `[]` if empty. When you DO pass a layout, `style` and
`columnCount` are REQUIRED -- `layouts[].style` is
load-bearing for rendering and omitting it produces an
unstyled dashboard. Use grid defaults `columnCount: 48`,
`rowHeight: 20`, `maxWidth: 1200`. 0-based row/column.

style.description:
REQUIRED for rendering -- always include a full style
block. Canonical defaults: `backgroundColor:
"#ffffff"`, `gutterColor: "#f3f3f3"`,
`cellSpacingX: 4`, `cellSpacingY: 4`.

pages.description:
Ordered pages in this layout. Set BOTH `name` (e.g.
`page_1`) and `label` on EVERY page inline here at create
time -- bulk-create does not auto-derive `page_N`, so an
omitted name breaks navigation targeting and an omitted
label renders a blank tab. Do NOT create the dashboard
then call `add_dashboard_page` just to name page one.

name.description:
Developer / API identifier for the page.
Alphanumeric + underscore, NO spaces. The platform
does NOT auto-derive `page_N` -- if omitted the page
is stored with no name, and any navigation widget
that targets it by `page_N` will not resolve. ALWAYS
set it (e.g. `page_1`, `page_2`, ... in order). Same
silent rename rules as the top-level dashboard
`name`.

label.description:
Page display name (free text). This is how you label
the FIRST page at create time -- set it here rather
than creating then calling `add_dashboard_page`.
ALWAYS set it: an unset label renders a blank page
tab. When the user gives no name, default to a
meaningful label from the dashboard's purpose (e.g.
"Overview"), never a bare "Page 1" placeholder.

name.description: Must match a key in the top-level `widgets` map.

update_dashboard.name: update_dashboard
update_dashboard.description:
Update an existing Tableau Next dashboard.

**⚠️ PREFER THE DEDICATED DASHBOARD TOOLS for single, targeted edits.**
`update_dashboard` is a FULL-REPLACEMENT PATCH -- it requires you to
re-send the ENTIRE `widgets` map and `layouts` array, and any field you
get wrong (orphaned widget keys, missing `style`, wrong `type` case)
silently corrupts rendering even though the PATCH returns 200. For
one-off operations, the purpose-built tools below perform the
read-modify-write for you atomically and are far less error-prone. Do
NOT hand-roll these through `update_dashboard`:

| To do this | Use this tool (NOT `update_dashboard`) |
|---|---|
| Add a widget (viz / text / filter / image / metric) and place it on the grid | `add_widget_to_dashboard` |
| Remove a single widget | `remove_widget_from_dashboard` |
| Add a page | `add_dashboard_page` |
| Remove a page | `remove_dashboard_page` |
| Add a global / interactive filter | `add_global_filter_to_dashboard` |

Reserve `update_dashboard` for BULK or STRUCTURAL changes the
single-purpose tools cannot express in one call (e.g. re-laying-out many
tiles at once, replacing a whole page's grid, or editing dashboard-level
`style` / `customConfig`).

**TL;DR:** `get_dashboard` first, mutate the returned `widgets` and `layouts`, send the FULL structures back. PATCH replaces, does NOT merge.

**Inputs:**
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (path)
- body containing `label` (REQUIRED -- display name),
  `workspaceIdOrApiName` (REQUIRED -- id like `1Dyxx...` or apiName,
  NOT the workspace label with spaces), `widgets` (REQUIRED -- FULL
  replacement map of widgetName -> widget), `layouts` (REQUIRED -- FULL
  replacement array). Optional: `description`, `style`, `customConfig`.

**PATCH semantics -- read, modify, write.** PATCH REPLACES, does NOT
merge. Always `get_dashboard` first, mutate the returned `widgets` and
`layouts`, send the FULL structures back.

- Sending only `widgets` (or only `layouts`) wipes the omitted side.
- `label` and `workspaceIdOrApiName` are required even when only
  changing widgets.

**Widget handle stability.** To keep an existing widget's source viz
intact across a PATCH, send back its same map key + same inner `name` +
same `source.{id, name}`. If you want to RENAME the handle, change all
three together. The `widget.id` (server-set Salesforce id) rotates on
every PATCH, so don't bind to it.

**Write shape is NOT the read shape.** Jackson is strict.

- These read-only fields cause 400 `Unrecognized field` if sent:
  `widget.source.label`, `widget.source.type`.
- These are server-set and rotate on every PATCH (bind to `.name`
  keys, not ids): `widget.id`, `widget.status`, `layouts[].id`,
  `pages[].id`, `pages[].widgets[].id`.
- `pages[].label` and `widget.label` ARE accepted on write.

**Widget type.** On write `widget.type` must be LOWERCASE
(`"visualization"` or `"text"`). The response and JSONSchema enum show
`"Visualization"` capitalized but that fails on input with
`Could not resolve type id 'Visualization'`.

**Widget-to-layout linkage.** Every key in `widgets` must equal that
widget's inner `name` AND must appear in some
`layouts[].pages[].widgets[].name`. Orphans silently corrupt rendering
(saves OK, renders blank or shifted).

**Grid.** 0-based coords. Modern defaults `columnCount: 48`,
`rowHeight: 20`, `maxWidth: 1200`. Half-width = `colspan: 24`,
full = `48`. Standard tile height = `rowspan: 20`.

- Side by side: tile A `{column: 0, colspan: 24}` + tile B
  `{column: 24, colspan: 24}` with same `row` and `rowspan`.
- Stacked: tile B `row = A.row + A.rowspan`.

**Layout style is load-bearing.** The Aura grid renderer dereferences
`layouts[].style.cellSpacingX` without null-check. Omitting the style
block crashes the dashboard with
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cellSpacingX')`
even though the PATCH succeeds. ALWAYS include:
```json
"style": {
  "backgroundColor": "#ffffff",
  "cellSpacingX": 4,
  "cellSpacingY": 4,
  "gutterColor": "#f3f3f3"
}
```

**Pages.** `pages[].name` required (any non-empty string; `"page_1"` is
conventional). `pages[].label` optional, free text.

**Widget-kind parameters.**

- Chart tile (`type: "visualization"`):
  ```json
  "parameters": {
    "legendPosition": "Right",
    "receiveFilterSource": {"filterMode": "all", "widgetIds": []}
  },
  "actions": []
  ```

- KPI tile: same `type: "visualization"`, named `kpi_<n>`. Parameters
  extends with `widgetStyle: {backgroundColor, borderColor, borderEdges:
  ["all"], borderRadius, borderWidth}`.

- Text widget (`type: "text"`, no `source`):
  ```json
  "parameters": {
    "conditionalFormattingRules": [],
    "content": <Quill delta -- array of {attributes, insert, rules}>,
    "receiveFilterSource": {...}
  }
  ```

**Minimal viable widget:**
```json
"visualization_0": {
  "name": "visualization_0",
  "type": "visualization",
  "source": {"id": "<vizId>", "name": "<vizApiName>"},
  "parameters": {
    "legendPosition": "Right",
    "receiveFilterSource": {"filterMode": "all", "widgetIds": []}
  },
  "actions": []
}
```

**Minimal viable layout:**
```json
[{
  "name": "default",
  "columnCount": 48,
  "rowHeight": 20,
  "maxWidth": 1200,
  "style": {
    "backgroundColor": "#ffffff",
    "cellSpacingX": 4,
    "cellSpacingY": 4,
    "gutterColor": "#f3f3f3"
  },
  "pages": [{
    "name": "page_1",
    "label": "Overview",
    "widgets": [{
      "name": "visualization_0",
      "row": 0, "column": 0,
      "rowspan": 20, "colspan": 24
    }]
  }]
}]
```

**Common 400 errors.**

- `MasterLabel missing` -- top-level `label` was omitted.
- `Workspace name is missing` -- top-level `workspaceIdOrApiName` was
  omitted.
- `Could not resolve type id 'Visualization'` -- `widget.type` was
  capitalized; use lowercase.
- `Unrecognized field 'label'` at a write payload -- almost always
  `widget.source.label` (NOT `pages[].label`, which IS accepted).
  Strip `source.label` and `source.type` and retry.

**Returns:** parsed dashboard metadata directly as a flat JSON object
-- `update_dashboard` is NOT double-wrapped (distinct from
`create_dashboard` and `create_*_viz`, which ARE double-wrapped). The
wrapping is per-tool, NOT family-wide; do not assume.

**Use when:** you need BULK or STRUCTURAL changes in a single PATCH --
reordering or resizing many tiles at once, swapping a whole page's
layout, or editing dashboard-level `style` / `customConfig`. For a
SINGLE widget, page, or filter operation, use the dedicated tools
listed at the top of this doc instead -- they are atomic and avoid the
full-replacement footguns below.

**Typical flow:** `get_dashboard` -> mutate widgets / layouts ->
`update_dashboard`.

Minor version supported for the API. Always send `-1` (latest
supported minor version) -- the single-value enum forces this
so a compliant client always emits it and can only pick the
one allowed value. NOT a dashboard revision. See
createDashboard.yaml / showDashboard.yaml for the same pattern
rationale.

label.description: Display name. Required even when only changing widgets.

widgets.description:
FULL replacement map of widgetName -> widget. Sending only
`widgets` (or only `layouts`) wipes the omitted side. Each
entry is `{ "type": "<lowercase widget type>", "name":
"<unique widget key>", "source": { "id": "<viz id>",
"name": "<viz apiName>" } }`. Lowercase `type` on write
-- one of "visualization", "text", "filter", "image",
"metric", "button", "container", "extension", "summary",
"parameter". Strip `source.label` / `source.type`. Every
key must equal its inner `name` and appear in
`layouts[].pages[].widgets[]`.

name.description:
Page developer / API name. Alphanumeric +
underscore, NO spaces. Optional -- if omitted
the platform derives `page_N`. Same silent
rename rules as the top-level dashboard `name`.

label.description:
Page display name. Free text. Optional. PATCH
REPLACES pages wholesale, so on a
get->mutate->update round-trip you MUST send the
page label back here or it is dropped. Omit for
an unlabeled page.

delete_dashboard.name: delete_dashboard
delete_dashboard.description:
Delete a Tableau Next dashboard permanently.

**Inputs:**
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (path) -- the id or apiName from
  `list_dashboards` or `browse_data_assets`.

**Returns:** confirmation of deletion.

**Use when:** you need to permanently remove a dashboard and all its
widget references. DESTRUCTIVE -- there is no undo.

**Scope:** current org only.

**Caveats:**

- **Not idempotent.** A second call returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (404)
  -- treat as success-equivalent if you may double-call.

- **Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
  `{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}`.
  Parse `JSON.parse(response.defaultExc)` to get the body. EXCEPTION:
  on 204 success, `defaultExc` is the literal string `"204"` (NOT
  JSON-parseable). Branch on `responseCode === 204` for the success
  path.

list_visualizations.name: list_visualizations
list_visualizations.description:
Enumerate visualizations / worksheets (metadata only) across Tableau
Next.

**Inputs:** optional `limit`, `offset`, `minorVersion`.

**Returns:** a `visualizations[]` array (NOT `items[]` -- the response key
is tool-specific despite the family-wide pattern) with id, name / label,
parent dashboard / workbook, owning workspace, and timestamps.

**Use when:** you need to discover charts / worksheets by name or
parent.

**Do NOT use when:**
- you want one full viz definition -> `get_visualization`

**Scope:** current org only. There is NO workspace or SDM filter -- the
tool returns every visualization the caller can see across the org,
mixing all workspaces. To list visualizations scoped to a single
workspace, use `list_workspace_assets`; otherwise filter client-side by
reading viz metadata if scope matters.

minorVersion.description: Minor API version for visualization operations.

get_visualization.name: get_visualization
get_visualization.description:
Retrieve a single visualization bundle with the semantic model inlined
directly on its data source (`semanticModel` / `useInlineModel` populated),
so the model comes back without a second round trip.

**Inputs:**
- `visualizationIdOrApiName` (path) -- the id or apiName from
  `list_visualizations` or `browse_data_assets`. Either works -- both
  pre-existing and freshly-created ids resolve via this tool.
- `minorVersion` (query) -- Minor API version to read at. Defaults to `-1`
  (latest deployed patch); leave it at the default unless you need to pin an
  older version. Do not skip it -- an absent value reads at minor version `0`.

**Returns:** Full visualization metadata rendered as an interactive widget.

**Use when:** user asks to show, view, or display a specific visualization
by name or ID. This tool directly renders the visualization — do NOT chain
to `render_visualization`.

**Closed-loop create-then-read works.** Ids returned by `create_timeseries_viz`,
`create_comparative_viz`, `create_compositional_viz`, and
`create_relationship_viz` are immediately retrievable via this tool by
either `id` or `name` (apiName). If you previously saw `NOT_FOUND` on a
fresh id, that was a transient bug; the tool is reliable as of this
release.

create_visualization.name: create_visualization
create_visualization.description:
Create a Tableau Next visualization from a slim IR-v2 spec. The server
hydrates everything else (full style scaffold, legends, marks.headers,
marks.fields per continuous-axis fieldKey, view, interactions, per-field
type and inferred role, referenceLines, measureValues).

This is the single entry point for authoring any Tableau Next chart:
bars (incl. stacked, grouped, and multi-measure), lines, donut,
scatter/bubble (Circle + Size), heatmaps (`Square`), text, and Table
layout. Schema mirrors Brett Webber's IR-v2 minimal shape from the
`bwebber/viz-metadata-optional` analytics-ui PR.

# Required body fields

- `label` — display name for the visualization (free text).
- `workspaceId` — workspace Id (e.g. `0Za...`). Get from
  `list_workspaces` (`id` field).
- `workspaceName` — workspace API name (no spaces). Get from
  `list_workspaces` (`name` field). Do NOT pass the label-with-spaces.
- `semanticModelName` — SDM API name. Get from
  `list_semantic_models` or `get_semantic_model` (`name` field).
- `semanticModelLabel` — SDM display label. Get from
  `list_semantic_models` or `get_semantic_model` (`label` field).
- `fields` — map of `fieldKey -> field binding` (see below).
- `visualSpecification` — minimal viz spec (see below).

# `fields` (map of fieldKey -> binding)

Pick caller-chosen fieldKey strings (e.g. `F1`, `F2`, or
`region_dim`, `sales_meas`). They must exactly match the fieldKey
strings used in `visualSpecification.rows`, `columns`, and any
`encodings`.

Per-field shape:

```json
{
  "objectName": "<sdm_data_object_api_name>",  // omit for a model-level calculated measure — see Rules
  "fieldName": "<column_api_name>",
  "displayCategory": "Discrete | Continuous",
  "function": "<aggregation_or_date_function>",  // optional
  "level": "Row | AggregateFunction | TableCalc | Lod",  // required for an aggregated model-level calc
  "numberFormat": "Currency | Percent | Abbreviated | Precise",  // optional, measures only
  "referenceLine": "Average | Sum | Min | Max | Target",         // optional, measures only
  "referenceLineValue": 1000000,                                 // required iff referenceLine=Target
  "colorScale": "Diverging"                                      // optional, Color-encoded measure
}
```

Rules:

- `objectName` + `fieldName` identify the field to bind:
  - For a field that lives on a data object — a raw dimension or raw
    measure, i.e. anything returned by `list_semantic_model_dimensions`
    / `list_semantic_model_measures` — pass BOTH `objectName` (the data
    object api name) and `fieldName`.
  - For a **model-level calculated measure** — one returned by
    `list_semantic_model_calculated_measures`, which has an `expression`
    and does NOT belong to any single data object — pass ONLY
    `fieldName` (the calc measure's api name) and **omit `objectName`**.
    Binding a calc measure with an `objectName` makes the backend fail
    at create time with a generic `UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION`; dropping
    `objectName` resolves it cleanly. Copy the calc measure's `level`
    returned by `list_semantic_model_calculated_measures` into the
    field's `level` property whenever `function` is supplied, then choose
    `function` from that level:
    - For `AggregateFunction` and `TableCalc`, use `UserAgg`.
    - For `Row` and `Lod` (LOD), do **not** use `UserAgg`; use the ordinary
      aggregation appropriate for its `aggregationType` (`Average` maps
      to `Avg`, `CountDistinct` maps to `CountD`), or omit `function`
      when the aggregation type is `Auto` or `None`.
    The server rejects missing or incompatible level/function pairs
    before saving the visualization.
- `displayCategory`:
  - `Continuous` for measures, and for `DateTrunc*` date dimensions.
  - `Discrete` for plain dimensions, and for `DatePart*` date
    dimensions.
- `function` (optional, drives display labels and the server's role
  inference — Measure if any aggregation function is set, otherwise
  Dimension):
  - Measures: `Sum`, `Avg`, `Median`, `Count`, `CountD`, `Min`,
    `Max`, `UserAgg`.
  - Continuous date dimensions: `DateTruncYear`, `DateTruncQuarter`,
    `DateTruncMonth`, `DateTruncWeek`, `DateTruncDay`.
  - Discrete date dimensions: `DatePartYear`, `DatePartQuarter`,
    `DatePartMonth`, `DatePartWeek`, `DatePartDay`.
  - Fiscal-calendar date dimensions (anchored to the org's fiscal
    year, no Day granularity): `FiscalDateTruncYear`,
    `FiscalDateTruncQuarter`, `FiscalDateTruncMonth`,
    `FiscalDateTruncWeek` (Continuous) and `FiscalDatePartYear`,
    `FiscalDatePartQuarter`, `FiscalDatePartMonth`,
    `FiscalDatePartWeek` (Discrete).
  - Plain dimensions: omit.

The server fills `type: "Field"` automatically and infers `role` from
`function`/`displayCategory`.

## Best-practice formatting (mostly automatic)

The server already applies professional defaults so a basic spec
renders cleanly — you usually do NOT need the knobs below:

- **Numbers are abbreviated** — `NumberShort` with `K`/`M`/`B` units,
  1 decimal place (0 for `Count`/`CountD`). Axes read `$1.2M`-style,
  not `1234567.89`.
- **Bars are auto-sorted** — a bar chart with one categorical
  (non-date) dimension and one measure is sorted by the measure
  **descending** ("unsorted bars are nearly useless"). Date axes stay
  chronological; charts with 2+ shelf dimensions or 2+ measures are
  left unsorted (ambiguous key).

Set these per-field knobs only to override:

- `numberFormat` (measures): `Currency` (`"$1.2M"`, assumes USD),
  `Percent` (a ratio **already stored 0–1** → `"45.2%"`; do NOT use on
  a value stored as `45.2`), `Abbreviated` (force K/M/B — the default),
  `Precise` (full digits `1,234,567`, no abbreviation).
- `referenceLine` (measures): `Average`/`Sum`/`Min`/`Max` (computed
  line — e.g. `Average` turns a ranking into "vs. the mean"), or
  `Target` with `referenceLineValue` (a constant quota/threshold).
  There is no `Median`. Keep to at most one per chart.
- `colorScale` (a measure on a Color encoding): `Diverging` — a
  blue↔red ramp with a neutral midpoint, for signed / around-a-target
  measures (profit, variance, YoY change). Only when the measure is
  genuinely centered on zero/a target; on all-positive data it misleads.

And the top-level `sortIntent` overrides the auto-sort:
`MeasureDescending` | `MeasureAscending` | `DimensionAscending` |
`DimensionDescending` | `None`. Use `DimensionAscending` for lookup
tables (A→Z is the point) and `None` to preserve data order.

# filters

Optional array of filter clauses to persist into the visualization. Each
filter targets a fieldKey that must match a key in the `fields` map.
Dimension filters use In/NotIn operators; value ranges and date ranges use
Between (two bounds) or GreaterThanOrEqualTo/LessThanOrEqualTo (one bound).

Filtering follows the field's role, matching how the platform persists
filters:

- A filter on a **raw field** (no aggregation function) filters ROWS
  (a WHERE clause) — e.g. `Processing_Fee between 0 and 21`.
- A filter on an **aggregated measure** (the field carries a function
  like Sum/Avg/Count) filters aggregated GROUPS (a HAVING clause) —
  e.g. `SUM(Refund_Amount) between 100 and 500`.

You do not choose the bucket; it is derived from the field. Filters
compose with `excludeNulls` (which adds its own aggregated null filter)
without clobbering.

Filter shape:

```json
{
  "fieldKey": "<field_key_string>",
  "type": "Dimension | ValueRange | DateRange",
  "include": ["<value1>", "<value2>"],   // Dimension include (show only these)
  "exclude": ["<value3>", "<value4>"],   // Dimension exclude (hide these)
  "min": <number>,                       // ValueRange min (inclusive)
  "max": <number>,                       // ValueRange max (inclusive)
  "dateStart": "<ISO_date_string>",      // DateRange start (inclusive)
  "dateEnd": "<ISO_date_string>",        // DateRange end (inclusive)
  "includeNulls": <boolean>              // Dimension filters only, default false
}
```

Rules:

- **Dimension filters**: specify exactly one of `include` or `exclude`
  (not both, not neither). Values are matched against the dimension's
  distinct values. Set `includeNulls: true` to keep null dimension
  values in the result; default false excludes them.
- **ValueRange filters**: specify at least one of `min` or `max`. When
  both are present, emits a Between clause; when only one, emits
  GreaterThanOrEqualTo (min only) or LessThanOrEqualTo (max only) — the
  bounds are inclusive. If both are set, `min` must be ≤ `max`.
- **DateRange filters**: specify at least one of `dateStart` or
  `dateEnd` (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or full timestamp). Emits a
  date Between / GreaterThanOrEqualTo / LessThanOrEqualTo clause
  (inclusive bounds). Bounds must be real calendar dates — a malformed
  value like `2025-99-99` is rejected up front.
- **`includeNulls` applies to Dimension filters only.** On a
  `ValueRange`/`DateRange` filter it is ignored (range filters always
  exclude nulls).
- **Range filters require a Continuous field.** A `ValueRange`/`DateRange`
  on a `Discrete` (string) dimension is rejected — use a Dimension
  (include/exclude) filter for those.
- **Filtering a sorted dimension keeps the sort.** A bar chart auto-sorts
  its single categorical dimension by the measure. Filtering that
  dimension no longer drops the sort — the filter is applied on a
  separate internal copy so the sort and the filter coexist. (Filtering
  the *measure* the chart sorts by still drops the auto-sort, since a
  measure cannot be both a sort key and a filter target.)

## Filter examples

### Dimension include (show only selected categories)

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "fieldKey": "F1",
      "type": "Dimension",
      "include": ["Technology", "Furniture"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Persists a filter with operator `In` and values `["Technology", "Furniture"]`.
The saved viz shows only those two categories.

### Dimension exclude (hide selected regions)

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "fieldKey": "F2",
      "type": "Dimension",
      "exclude": ["South"],
      "includeNulls": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Persists a filter with operator `NotIn` and values `["South"]`. The chart
hides the South region.

### Value range on a raw field (row filter / WHERE)

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "fieldKey": "F3",
      "type": "ValueRange",
      "min": 1000,
      "max": 5000
    }
  ]
}
```

When `F3` is a raw field (no aggregation function), this persists a
`Between` clause into `filter` (WHERE) with values `[1000, 5000]`. Rows
whose `F3` value falls outside that range are excluded.

### Value range on an aggregated measure (group filter / HAVING)

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "fieldKey": "F2",
      "type": "ValueRange",
      "min": 100
    }
  ]
}
```

When `F2` is an aggregated measure (e.g. `Sum` of Refund Amount), this
persists a `GreaterThanOrEqualTo` clause into `aggregateFilter` (HAVING)
against the aggregation expression (e.g. `SUM([Object].[Refund_Amount])`).
Only groups whose aggregated total is ≥ 100 are kept. (Omitting `max`
yields the one-sided lower bound.)

### Date range (orders in 2025)

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "fieldKey": "F4",
      "type": "DateRange",
      "dateStart": "2025-01-01",
      "dateEnd": "2025-12-31"
    }
  ]
}
```

Persists a date `Between` filter. The viz shows only orders within 2025.

# forecasts (optional)

Optional map of `forecastKey -> forecast config`. Enables callers to pass
forecast settings: which measure to forecast, how far into the future
(horizon), and seasonality/confidence-interval options. Each forecast
targets a timeseries chart (Line mark with a continuous date dimension on
columns/rows) and produces a forecast line extending beyond the historical
data.

Forecasts require a timeseries **Line** chart with a continuous date
dimension (a `DateTrunc*` field). The forecast config is validated and the
forecast line renders in the saved visualization — see the validation rules
below.

Per-forecast config:

```json
{
  "forecastModel": "HoltWinters | RidgeRegression",
  "dimensionFields": [
    {
      "dateDim": {
        "fieldKey": "<continuous_date_dimension_fieldKey>",
        "granularity": "InferFromData"
      }
    }
  ],
  "measureFieldKey": "<measure_fieldKey>",
  "from": {
    "predefinedDate": "LatestData"
  },
  "to": {
    "forecastInterval": {
      "value": <integer>,
      "timeUnit": "Minutes | Hours | Days | Weeks | Months | Quarters | Years"
    }
  },
  "includeBounds": <boolean>,
  "confidenceLevel": 90 | 95 | 99,
  "ignoreLastPeriods": <integer>,
  "fillNullsWithZero": <boolean>
}
```

Rules:

- **forecastModel**: `HoltWinters` (exponential smoothing, handles seasonality
  and trend) or `RidgeRegression` (linear model with L2 regularization).
- **dimensionFields**: Array with one entry — the continuous date dimension
  (DateTrunc* function) that forms the timeseries axis. The `fieldKey` must
  match a key in the `fields` map that has `displayCategory: "Continuous"`
  and a `DateTrunc*` function. `granularity: "InferFromData"` is currently
  the only supported value (richer seasonality knobs are a further platform
  ask).
- **measureFieldKey**: Must match a key in the `fields` map that is a measure
  (has an aggregation function like `Sum`, `Avg`, etc.). The measure to
  forecast.
- **from**: Start point for the forecast. `predefinedDate: "LatestData"`
  begins forecasting from the latest date in the data.
- **to**: Forecast horizon. `forecastInterval.value` (must be > 0) specifies
  how many time units into the future to forecast, and `timeUnit` specifies
  the unit (`Minutes`, `Hours`, `Days`, `Weeks`, `Months`, `Quarters`, or
  `Years`).
- **includeBounds**: Optional, default true. Include confidence interval bounds
  (upper/lower bands around the forecast line).
- **confidenceLevel**: Optional, default 95. Confidence level for the forecast
  bounds. 90, 95, or 99 percent.
- **ignoreLastPeriods**: Optional, default 0. Number of trailing periods to
  exclude from the forecast model (useful if recent data is incomplete).
- **fillNullsWithZero**: Optional, default false. Treat null values in the
  historical data as zero.

**Timeseries-only**: Forecasts are only valid on Line charts with a continuous
date dimension (DateTrunc*) on the timeseries axis. Attempting to forecast a
non-timeseries chart (e.g. Bar with a categorical dimension) will fail with
`INVALID_INPUT`.

**Fields-map validation**: Both `dateDim.fieldKey` and `measureFieldKey` must
exist in the `fields` map and have the appropriate types (continuous date
dimension and measure, respectively). Referencing a missing or mistyped field
will fail with `INVALID_INPUT`.

## Forecast example (HoltWinters 6-month Line chart)

```json
{
  "label": "Sales Forecast — Next 6 Months",
  "workspaceId": "0Za...",
  "workspaceName": "MyWorkspace",
  "semanticModelName": "SalesSDM",
  "semanticModelLabel": "Sales SDM",
  "fields": {
    "F1": {
      "objectName": "Orders",
      "fieldName": "Order_Date",
      "displayCategory": "Continuous",
      "function": "DateTruncMonth"
    },
    "F2": {
      "objectName": "Orders",
      "fieldName": "Sales",
      "displayCategory": "Continuous",
      "function": "Sum"
    }
  },
  "visualSpecification": {
    "rows": ["F2"],
    "columns": ["F1"],
    "marks": {
      "panes": {
        "type": "Line"
      }
    },
    "forecasts": {
      "FC1": {
        "forecastModel": "HoltWinters",
        "dimensionFields": [
          {
            "dateDim": {
              "fieldKey": "F1",
              "granularity": "InferFromData"
            }
          }
        ],
        "measureFieldKey": "F2",
        "from": {
          "predefinedDate": "LatestData"
        },
        "to": {
          "forecastInterval": {
            "value": 6,
            "timeUnit": "Months"
          }
        },
        "includeBounds": true,
        "confidenceLevel": 95,
        "ignoreLastPeriods": 0,
        "fillNullsWithZero": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

# `visualSpecification` (slim — server hydrates the rest)

Required:

- `rows` — array of fieldKey strings on the rows shelf.
- `columns` — array of fieldKey strings on the columns shelf.
- `marks.panes.type` — one of `Bar`, `Line`, `Circle`, `Square`,
  `Text`, `Donut`.

Optional (omit when not deviating from server defaults):

- `layout` — defaults to `Vizql` when omitted.
- `marks.panes.encodings` — array of `{ fieldKey, type }`. `type` ∈
  { `Color`, `Label`, `Tooltip`, `Detail`, `Size`, `Range`, `Angle` }.
  Use `Color` for series with ≤10 distinct values, `Detail` for
  higher cardinality.
- `marks.panes.stack` — `{ isAutomatic: false, isStacked: <bool> }`
  to override the default. Default by mark type: Bar → stacked,
  others → not stacked.

The server fills (don't include unless overriding):

- `marks.headers` (default Text mark)
- `marks.fields` (one entry per continuous-axis fieldKey on rows/columns)
- `legends` (auto-derived from Color encodings)
- `referenceLines` (`{}`)
- `measureValues` (`[]`)
- `style` (full default scaffold — fonts, shading, lines, fieldLabels,
  encodings, headers, axis, marks)
- `view` (default empty view)
- `interactions` (`[]`)

# Mark type → chart shape

| Mark | What it makes | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Bar` | Bar chart | Discrete on rows = horizontal; on columns = vertical. Default stacking. |
| `Line` | Line chart | Temporal/ordinal dim on columns, measure on rows. |
| `Circle` | Scatter / bubble | Two measures on rows/columns. Add `Size` encoding for bubble. |
| `Square` | Heatmap | Two discrete dims + a `Color` encoding mapped to a measure. |
| `Text` | Single value / text marks | Measure on `Label`, or a 0-dimension grand total. |
| `Donut` | Donut chart | Set `layout: "Radial"`, empty rows/columns. `Angle` encoding for the measure + `Color` for the dimension. |

For a tabular crosstab, set `visualSpecification.layout: "Table"`, put
the grouping dimensions in `groups` (outer→inner) and the measures in
`rows`; every field renders as a discrete text column (`marks.panes.type`
is ignored).

```json
    "F3": {"objectName": "Orders", "fieldName": "Profit",     "displayCategory": "Continuous", "function": "Sum"}
  },
  "visualSpecification": {
    "rows": ["F1"],
    "columns": ["F2", "F3"],
    "marks": {"panes": {"type": "Line"}}
  }
}
```

## 8. Donut chart

Empty `rows`/`columns`. Measure goes on `Angle`, dimension on `Color`.

```json
{
  "label": "Sales by Category",
  "workspaceId": "0Za...",
  "workspaceName": "MyWorkspace",
  "semanticModelName": "SalesSDM",
  "semanticModelLabel": "Sales SDM",
  "fields": {
    "F1": {"objectName": "Orders", "fieldName": "Category", "displayCategory": "Discrete"},
    "F2": {"objectName": "Orders", "fieldName": "Sales",    "displayCategory": "Continuous", "function": "Sum"}
  },
  "visualSpecification": {
    "rows": [],
    "columns": [],
    "marks": {
      "panes": {
        "type": "Donut",
        "encodings": [
          {"type": "Angle", "fieldKey": "F2"},
          {"type": "Color", "fieldKey": "F1"}
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "workspaceId": "0Za...",

  "semanticModelName": "SalesSDM",
```
