## 10. Calculated-measure bar chart (omit `objectName`)

Binding a model-level calculated measure (from
`list_semantic_model_calculated_measures`). Note `F2` has a
`fieldName` but **no `objectName`** — that is what makes it resolve;
the dimension `F1` is a normal data-object field and keeps both. This
example assumes `MRR_Loss_Ratio` has level `AggregateFunction` or
`TableCalc`, so its function is `UserAgg`. For a `Row` or `Lod` (LOD)
calculated measure, use its ordinary aggregation instead.

```json
{
  "label": "Loss Ratio by Reason",
  "workspaceId": "0Za...",
  "workspaceName": "MyWorkspace",
  "semanticModelName": "ChurnSDM",
  "semanticModelLabel": "Churn SDM",
  "fields": {
    "F1": {"objectName": "fact_churn", "fieldName": "Churn_Reason",   "displayCategory": "Discrete"},
    "F2": {"fieldName": "MRR_Loss_Ratio", "displayCategory": "Continuous", "level": "AggregateFunction", "function": "UserAgg"}
  },
  "visualSpecification": {
    "rows": ["F2"],
    "columns": ["F1"],
    "marks": {"panes": {"type": "Bar"}}
  }
}
```

# What you'll get back

The server returns the saved visualization's identifying triple
(`id`, `label`, `name`). To inspect the full hydrated body (style,
legends, marks.fields), GET the visualization by id with
`get_visualization`.

# Common errors

- `INVALID_INPUT` — your payload omitted a top-level required field
  (`workspaceId`, `workspaceName`, `semanticModelName`,
  `semanticModelLabel`, `label`, `fields`, or `visualSpecification`), or
  a filter clause is malformed (e.g. a Dimension filter with both
  `include` and `exclude`, a ValueRange with `min` > `max`, or a
  DateRange with both `dateStart` and `dateEnd` empty).
- `INVALID_VISUALIZATION_METADATA` — a fieldKey on rows/columns/encodings
  or in a filter clause isn't present in the `fields` map, or the
  encoding type is not valid for the mark type (e.g. `Angle` only makes
  sense on `Donut`).
- `INVALID_INPUT` (forecast cases) — a forecast in `visualSpecification.forecasts`
  references a `measureFieldKey` or `dateDim.fieldKey` that is absent from the
  `fields` map, or a field with the wrong type (a measure fieldKey that is not a
  measure-role field, or a dateDim fieldKey that is not a continuous DateTrunc*
  date dimension); is placed on a non-timeseries chart (only a `Line` pane is
  allowed); has `to.forecastInterval.value` <= 0; or has a `confidenceLevel` that
  is not one of {90, 95, 99}. The error message names the offending forecastKey
  and field.
- `JSON_PARSER_ERROR` — body shape doesn't match the slim spec; check
  that `fields` is a map (not an array) and `visualSpecification` is
  an object (not nested under `body`).
- `UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION` — a generic backend error at create time, carrying
  an `ErrorId`. The most common, fixable cause is a field binding the
  backend can't resolve: binding a **model-level calculated measure**
  (one from `list_semantic_model_calculated_measures`) WITH an
  `objectName`. A calc measure is not a column on any data object, so
  drop `objectName` and pass only its `fieldName` (see Rules). Raw
  dimensions and measures still require both `objectName` and
  `fieldName`.

excludeNulls.description:
When true, exclude rows where a measure value is null, so the
chart hides cells/bars/lines backed by null measures. Defaults
to false (matches Tableau Next's default rendering — nulls are
kept).

Useful when the data has sparse measures (e.g. "show me sales
by region but skip regions with no sales reported"). The server
realizes this as an `IsNotNull` aggregate filter over each
measure-role fieldKey; the exact internal filter shape is an
implementation detail and may change.

fields.description:
Map of caller-chosen fieldKey → field binding. The fieldKeys
here must exactly match the strings used in
`visualSpecification.rows`, `columns`, and any encodings.

additionalProperties.description: Field binding for one fieldKey. The fieldKey itself is the map key in CreateBasicVizInputRepresentation.fields.

axisTitle.description:
Optional custom axis title for a MEASURE fieldKey on a shelf
(rows/columns). Overrides the default axis label (the measure
name) with readable text, e.g. "Profit ($)" or "Revenue (USD,
millions)". Maps to style.axis.fields[k].titleText. Ignored for
fieldKeys that are not on a continuous axis.

colorScale.description:
Optional palette intent when this MEASURE fieldKey is on a
Color encoding (ignored otherwise):
  - Diverging — a two-ended palette with a neutral midpoint, for
    signed or around-a-target measures (profit, variance,
    YoY change), so positive and negative read distinctly. Uses
    a colorblind-safe blue↔red ramp (never red/green). Only set
    this when the measure is genuinely centered on zero/a target;
    on an all-positive measure a diverging ramp misleads.
Maps to style.encodings.fields[k].colors (Continuous gradient).

displayCategory.description:
Continuous for measures and DateTrunc* date dimensions.
Discrete for plain dimensions and DatePart* date dimensions.

fieldName.description:
SDM field API name on `objectName` (e.g. "Sales"). Required for
`Field` type; omit for MeasureNames/MeasureValues synthetic fields.

function.description:
Optional aggregation or date function (drives display labels
and the server's role inference — Measure if any aggregation
function is set, otherwise Dimension).

Aggregations: Sum, Avg, Median, Count, CountD, Min, Max.
Continuous date trunc: DateTruncYear, DateTruncQuarter,
DateTruncMonth, DateTruncWeek, DateTruncDay.
Discrete date part: DatePartYear, DatePartQuarter,
DatePartMonth, DatePartWeek, DatePartDay.
Fiscal variants (no Day): FiscalDateTruncYear/Quarter/Month/Week
and FiscalDatePartYear/Quarter/Month/Week.
Plain dimensions: omit.

level.description:
Authoritative semantic calculation level for a model-level
calculated measure returned by
list_semantic_model_calculated_measures. Omit for fields that
belong to a data object. Required when a model-level calculated
measure supplies an aggregation function so the server can reject
incompatible combinations before saving:
  - AggregateFunction / TableCalc require UserAgg.
  - Row / Lod (LOD) reject UserAgg and accept ordinary
    aggregation functions.

numberFormat.description:
Optional display-format intent for a MEASURE fieldKey
(ignored on dimensions). The server already abbreviates large
numbers by default (NumberShort + K/M/B auto units, 1 decimal;
0 decimals for Count/CountD). Set this only to override:
  - Currency — money: "$1.2M" (CurrencyShort + "$" prefix).
    Assumes USD; the server does not infer currency from data.
  - Percent — a ratio ALREADY stored as a 0–1 fraction renders
    as "45.2%". Do NOT use on a value stored as 45.2 (it would
    show "4520%"); for that, leave default or use Precise.
  - Abbreviated — force K/M/B short form (this is the default
    for shelf measures; explicit here for clarity).
  - Precise — full digits with thousands separators
    ("1,234,567"), no abbreviation. Use for analyst/exact views.

objectName.description:
SDM data object API name (e.g. "Orders"). Required for `Field`
type; omit for MeasureNames/MeasureValues synthetic fields.

referenceLine.description:
Optional reference line on a MEASURE fieldKey (ignored on
dimensions). Draws a single line scoped to the pane:
  - Average / Sum / Min / Max — a computed line over the
    measure (e.g. Average turns a ranking into "vs. the mean").
    Median is NOT supported by the engine.
  - Target — a constant line at `referenceLineValue` (e.g. a
    quota or threshold); requires referenceLineValue to be set.
Keep to at most one reference line per chart — they are a
finishing touch, not a pile-on. Maps to
visualSpecification.referenceLines.

referenceLineValue.description:
The constant value for a `Target` reference line (e.g. a sales
quota of 1000000). Required when referenceLine=Target; ignored
for the computed kinds (Average/Sum/Min/Max).

type.description:
Field kind. Defaults to `Field` when omitted.
  - Field — a normal SDM-backed field (dimension or measure);
    requires objectName + fieldName.
  - MeasureNames / MeasureValues — synthetic fields for a
    shared-axis multi-measure chart (multiple measures on ONE
    value axis, distinguished by color). They bind no SDM
    column, so objectName/fieldName are omitted. Use the pair
    together with visualSpecification.measureValues, which lists
    the real measure fieldKeys: put the MeasureValues field on
    the shelf (rows/columns) and the MeasureNames field on a
    Color encoding. See IR_CHART_SPEC_V2 "Multi-Measure Charts".

filters.description:
Optional array of dimension and measure filter clauses.
Dimension filters persist as view.viewSpecification.filter
(In/NotIn operators); value and date ranges persist as
Between/GreaterThanOrEqualTo/LessThanOrEqualTo. Each filter's fieldKey must
match a key in the `fields` map. Composes with excludeNulls
(which writes aggregateFilter, a separate bucket).

items.description:
Filter clause for a dimension or measure field. The fieldKey must
match a key in the `fields` map. Every filter type (Dimension,
ValueRange, DateRange) routes by FIELD ROLE, not by filter type:
a filter on a raw/unaggregated field writes
view.viewSpecification.filter (WHERE-level); a filter on an
aggregated measure writes view.viewSpecification.aggregateFilter
(HAVING-level).

dateEnd.description:
End date for a DateRange filter (inclusive). ISO 8601 format
(YYYY-MM-DD or full timestamp). For one-sided ranges, omit
dateStart. For two-sided, set both dateStart and dateEnd.

dateStart.description:
Start date for a DateRange filter (inclusive). ISO 8601 format
(YYYY-MM-DD or full timestamp). For one-sided ranges, omit
dateEnd. For two-sided, set both dateStart and dateEnd.

exclude.description:
Array of dimension values to EXCLUDE (hide these values).
Required for Dimension type with exclude semantics; omit for include.
Maps to view.viewSpecification.filter operator NotIn.

fieldKey.description: The fieldKey to filter, must match a key in the `fields` map.

include.description:
Array of dimension values to INCLUDE (show only these values).
Required for Dimension type with include semantics; omit for exclude.
Maps to view.viewSpecification.filter operator In.

includeNulls.description:
Whether to include null values in the filtered result (default false).
Applies to Dimension filters; maps to includeNulls in the persisted
filter clause.

max.description:
Maximum value for a ValueRange filter (inclusive). For one-sided
ranges, omit min and set only max (LessThanOrEqualTo). For two-sided,
set both min and max (Between). Must be >= min when both are set.

min.description:
Minimum value for a ValueRange filter (inclusive). For one-sided
ranges, omit max and set only min (GreaterThanOrEqualTo). For two-sided,
set both min and max (Between). Must be <= max when both are set.

label.description: Display name for the visualization (free text).

sortIntent.description:
Optional override of the automatic sort. By default a bar
chart with one categorical (non-date) dimension and one
measure is sorted by the measure DESCENDING ("unsorted bars
are nearly useless"); date axes stay chronological and
ambiguous shelves (2+ dimensions or 2+ measures) are left
unsorted. Set this to deviate:
  - MeasureDescending / MeasureAscending — sort the dimension
    by the primary measure.
  - DimensionAscending / DimensionDescending — sort the
    dimension alphabetically/by its own value (e.g. a lookup
    table where A→Z order is the point).
  - None — leave unsorted (engine/data order).
Maps to view.viewSpecification.sortOrders. Applies to the
single categorical shelf dimension; ignored when there is no
unambiguous dimension+measure pair (e.g. scatter, multi-measure).

visualSpecification.description:
Slim visual specification. Server hydrates legends, referenceLines,
forecasts, measureValues, the full style scaffold, marks.headers,
and marks.fields per continuous-axis fieldKey.

For Vizql layout (default): supply `rows`, `columns`, and
`marks.panes.type`. For Radial layout: set `layout: "Radial"`,
omit `rows`/`columns`, and use `marks.panes.type: "Donut"` with
Angle + Color encodings. For Table layout: set `layout: "Table"`,
put the table's column dimensions in `groups` and the measures
(and any row dimensions) in `rows`; every field renders as a text
column. `marks.panes.type` is ignored for tables.

columns.description: FieldKeys on the columns axis. Required for Vizql; omitted for Radial/Table.

forecasts.description:
Optional map of caller-chosen forecastKey → forecast config
(e.g. {"FC1": {...}}). Each forecast adds a projected
forecast/trend line to a timeseries chart: a Line mark whose
single continuous date dimension (a DateTrunc* field) is the
x-axis and whose measure is the forecasted value. Requires
API version 262+.

When omitted the server emits an empty map (no forecast),
preserving prior behavior. See BasicVizForecastRepresentation
for the per-forecast shape; the config mirrors the canonical
visualization forecast input (min-version 254) already
persisted by the platform save pipeline.

additionalProperties.description:
A single forecast/trend line on a timeseries chart. Inlines the
canonical visualization forecast input shape
(BaseVisualizationForecastModelInputRepresentation, min-version
254, from unified-analytics-visualization.schema) so the slim
BasicViz author can request forecasts without a cross-module
schema reference. The two model kinds (HoltWinters, RidgeRegression)
share this identical property set — the `forecastModel` enum is the
only discriminator, and neither subtype adds fields.

confidenceLevel.description:
Confidence level for the bounds band, in percent. One of 90, 95,
or 99. Defaults to 95. Requires API version 258+.

dimensionFields.description:
The forecast's date dimension(s). Exactly one entry today,
wrapping the continuous date dimension fieldKey the forecast
projects along.

items.description: Wrapper for a forecast's date dimension field.

dateDim.description: The date dimension fieldKey + granularity for a forecast.

fieldKey.description:
The fieldKey (in `fields`) of the continuous date dimension
(a DateTrunc* field) used as the forecast x-axis.

granularity.description:
Forecast granularity. Only InferFromData is supported — the
engine infers the period from the data.

fillNullsWithZero.description:
Treat null values in the historical series as zero before
fitting. Defaults to false. Requires API version 258+.

forecastModel.description:
The forecast model. HoltWinters captures level+trend+seasonality
(best for data with a repeating cycle); RidgeRegression fits a
regularized linear trend (best for a smooth non-seasonal trend).

predefinedDate.description:
Where the forecast begins. Only LatestData is supported — the
forecast extends from the last historical data point.

ignoreLastPeriods.description:
Number of trailing time periods to exclude from the model fit
(useful when the most recent periods are incomplete). Defaults
to 0. Requires API version 258+.

includeBounds.description:
Whether to render the confidence-interval band (shaded area)
around the forecast line. Defaults to true when omitted.

measureFieldKey.description:
The fieldKey (in `fields`) of the measure being forecasted.
Must name a measure-role field (has an aggregation function).

forecastInterval.description: A forecast horizon expressed as value + time unit.

timeUnit.description: The time unit of the forecast horizon.

value.description: The number of time units to forecast forward. Must be > 0.

groups.description:
Table layout only. FieldKeys of the categorical dimensions that
form the table's grouping (leftmost dimension) columns, e.g.
["F1"] to group rows by Category. Ignored for Vizql/Radial.
Requires API version 262+.

layout.description:
Layout discriminator. Defaults to Vizql when omitted.
Table requires API version 262+ (its grouping columns use the
262-gated `groups` property; an ungrouped table still works at
262 with everything in `rows`).

markColor.description:
Optional single mark color for a chart with NO Color encoding
(one color for every bar/line/point). Accepts a CSS hex string —
either shorthand "#RGB" or full "#RRGGBB" (e.g. "#E8762D") — or a
common color name (orange, blue, red, green, purple, teal, gray,
black, etc.). Maps to style.marks.panes.color.color (and the
per-field mark cards). Ignored when the pane has a Color encoding —
there the palette owns the colors, so a single fixed color would be
meaningless. Leave unset to use the engine default (Tableau blue).

marks.description: Marks block. Only `panes` is required; the server synthesizes `headers` (default Text mark) and per-fieldKey `fields` entries for every continuous-axis fieldKey.

panes.description:
The default pane mark spec. Only `type` is required; the server
fills `isAutomatic`, `stack` (Bar→stacked, others→not), and
an empty `encodings` array. Provide `encodings` only when adding
a series (Color, Detail, Size, Angle, Label, Range, Tooltip).

encodings.description: Optional pane mark encodings (Color, Size, Detail, Angle, etc.).

items.description: One pane mark encoding. Use Color for series with ≤10 distinct values, Detail for higher cardinality, Size for bubble charts, Angle for radial slices, Label to show values on marks.

fieldKey.description: A fieldKey defined in the parent `fields` map.

type.description: The encoding role for this fieldKey on the pane mark.

stack.description:
Pane stack override. Omit to accept the mark-type default —
Bar → stacked, all others → not stacked. Set
`{ isAutomatic: false, isStacked: false }` to force grouped
bars; `{ isAutomatic: false, isStacked: true }` to force stacking
on a non-Bar mark.

isAutomatic.description: Whether stacking is automatic. Set to false to override.

type.description:
Pane mark type. Vizql layout: Bar | Line | Circle | Square |
Text. Radial layout: Donut.

measureValues.description:
Optional. The real measure fieldKeys to plot on a single SHARED
value axis (a "MeasureNames/MeasureValues" multi-measure chart),
e.g. ["F2", "F3"] for Sales + Profit on one axis. Each entry must
name a measure-role `Field`-typed fieldKey present in `fields`.
Supply this together with one MeasureNames and one MeasureValues
synthetic field (put MeasureValues on the shelf, MeasureNames on
Color). Leave unset for single-measure charts or the side-by-side
form (separate panes via multiple measures on rows/columns).

rows.description:
FieldKeys on the rows axis. Required for Vizql; omitted for
Radial. For Table: the measures (and any non-grouping row
dimensions) shown as table columns.

delete_visualization.name: delete_visualization
delete_visualization.description:
Delete a Tableau Next visualization permanently.

**Inputs:**
- `visualizationIdOrApiName` (path) -- the id or apiName from
  `list_visualizations` or `browse_data_assets`.

**Returns:** confirmation of deletion.

**Use when:** you need to permanently remove a visualization.
DESTRUCTIVE -- there is no undo.

**Note:** deleting a visualization referenced by a dashboard may leave a
broken widget; remove the widget reference via `update_dashboard` first
if needed.

**Scope:** current org only.

**Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
`{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}`. Parse
`JSON.parse(response.defaultExc)` to get the body. EXCEPTION: on 204
success, `defaultExc` is the literal string `"204"` (NOT JSON-parseable).
Branch on `responseCode === 204` for the success path.

visualizationIdOrApiName.description: The ID or API name of the visualization.

edit_visualization.name: edit_visualization
edit_visualization.description:
Apply one or more edit operations to a Tableau Next visualization definition and return the modified definition as JSON. A single call applies several operations in order. This tool renders the edited visualization inline (the result is shown to the user automatically), so do NOT call `render_visualization` afterward. It does NOT save: it only computes and shows the edited definition.

**MANDATORY — ALWAYS ASK TO SAVE.** This tool never persists. After every successful `edit_visualization` call — even small or chained edits — your very next reply MUST end by asking, verbatim: **"Do you want to save the visualization?"** Call `update_visualization` ONLY if the user then explicitly confirms (e.g. "yes", "save it"). NEVER save automatically or assume the user wants to save.

**Inputs.** Both arguments go inside a single-element `inputs` array — the call payload is `{"inputs": [{"visualizationId": "...", "editOperations": "..."}]}`, NOT the two fields at the top level. The `inputs` array always has exactly one element.

- `visualizationId` (string, REQUIRED) — The `id` of the visualization to edit: from `get_visualization`, or returned by a prior `edit_visualization`/`update_visualization`. The tool loads the working definition by id, so you do not send its metadata. If the tool reports the id was not found, call `get_visualization` with that id to reload it, then retry. For a visualization just made with `create_visualization`, first `get_visualization` by its returned `id` — `create_visualization` returns only `{id, label, name}`, not an editable bundle.
- `editOperations` (string, REQUIRED) — The operations to apply, as a JSON **string** (the operations array serialized to text — never a raw array). All-or-nothing: if any operation fails, none apply; each sees the previous one's result. Each entry is `{operationType, params}`. For a single change, pass a one-element array. See "Chaining Operations" below.

**Returns:** `visualizationMetadata` — the modified definition as a JSON string. To chain another edit, call `edit_visualization` again with the same `visualizationId` (it loads the just-edited state). To persist, call `update_visualization` with the same `visualizationId` — but only after the user confirms.

**Use when:** the user asks to add/remove/replace/change a field on rows or columns (including aggregation or discrete/continuous), rename the visualization, add/edit/remove a filter or forecast, sort, add/remove/replace a mark encoding (color, label, tooltip, size, detail), change the mark type, add/remove/synchronize a dual axis, add/remove/edit a reference line, apply/edit/remove a quick table calculation, or set/reset an axis title.

## Operation types

- addFieldToRowsOrColumns / removeFieldFromRowsOrColumns / replaceFieldFromRowsOrColumns — add, remove, or swap a field on the rows or columns shelf.
- changeFieldOnRowsOrColumns — change an existing shelf field's aggregation and/or discrete-vs-continuous display; does not add/remove/swap.
- changeLabel — rename the visualization (its name, not the title drawn on it).
- addFilter / editFilter / removeFilter — add, update, or remove a filter.
- addForecast / editForecast / removeForecast — forecast a measure over time; predict future values.
- sortAscending / sortDescending / sortByField / clearSort — sort a shelf field.
- addFieldToEncoding / removeFieldFromEncoding / replaceFieldOnEncoding — assign, remove, or swap a marks encoding slot (Color, Label, Tooltip, Size, Detail).
- changeMarkType — change the mark shape only (does not add or move fields).
- addDualAxis / removeDualAxis / synchronizeAxis — overlay two adjacent continuous fields on one pane with two axes, split them apart, or change how the axes relate.
- addReferenceLine / removeReferenceLine / editReferenceLine — a reference line on an axis field already on a shelf.
- applyTableCalc / editTableCalc / removeTableCalc — a quick table calculation on a measure already on a shelf.
- editAxisTitle / resetAxisTitle — set or reset a field's axis title.

## Common conventions

**Field object.** A field is `{fieldName, objectName?, function?}`. Filters instead reference fields as `{model: "Object.Field"}` or `{expression: "..."}` (see Filters). Encoding, dual-axis, reference-line, and rows/columns operations all nest the field under a `"field"` key (or named keys like `primaryField`, `targetField`, `existingField`/`newField`).

**`function`** sets aggregation or date bucketing — use these canonical `VisualizationFieldFunctionType` values, NEVER display words like "Year"/"Month":
- Aggregations: Sum, Avg, Median, Count, CountD, Min, Max, Stdev, Stdevp, Var, Varp, Attr. (Count/CountD/Min/Max also apply to dimensions; the rest are measures only.)
- Date parts (→ integer): DatePartYear, DatePartQuarter, DatePartMonth, DatePartWeek, DatePartDay, DatePartHour, DatePartMinute.
- Date truncations (→ date): DateTruncYear, DateTruncQuarter, DateTruncMonth, DateTruncWeek, DateTruncDay.
- Fiscal variants exist too (e.g. FiscalDatePartYear, FiscalDateTruncQuarter).
- Omit `function` to keep a measure's default aggregation. A date dimension on a shelf is bucketed by year, so use `DatePartYear` for "broken out by year"; for finer breakouts or date-part filtering use a DATEPART/DATETRUNC expression, not a shelf function.

**`occurrence`** (1-based) picks which copy when the same field sits on a shelf more than once under the same name/object/function. `function` alone distinguishes copies aggregated differently (Sum of Sales vs Avg of Sales).

**Semantic models** contain data objects (e.g. "Orders") with dimensions and measures. Reference a field for filters as `{model: "Orders.Region"}`; elsewhere nest `{field: {fieldName: "Region", objectName: "Orders"}}`.

**Logical views (incl. hierarchical).** Structure: `semanticLogicalViews[]` → `semanticUnions[]` → `semanticMappedFields[]`. When a field appears under a union, ALWAYS use the logical view's apiName as `objectName`, never the union's (the view is queryable; unions are internal). Example: field "Full_Name20" in Manager_Union44 → `objectName: "Manager_oh"`.
- Hierarchical logical views (HLV) expose hierarchy fields. Me/My-team filters use hardcoded API names — Manager hierarchy `SemanticManagerUserIdPath`, Role hierarchy `SemanticRoleUserIdPath`:
  - Me: `{filter: {fields: [{model: "Manager_oh.SemanticManagerUserIdPath"}], operator: "EndsWithIgnoreCase", values: ["{expression: USERID18()}"]}, bucket: "filter"}`
  - My team: same with `operator: "ContainsIgnoreCase"`.
- Level-based display: add `hierarchyLevel` — `{fieldName: "Full_Name", hierarchyLevel: 1, objectName: "Manager_oh", displayCategory: "Discrete", role: "Dimension", type: "Field"}`.
- Per-level filters use `ANCESTOR_AT_LEVEL`: `{expression: "ANCESTOR_AT_LEVEL(1, [Manager_oh].[Full_Name])", operator: "In", values: ["Sarah Chen (CEO)"]}`.

## Field placement (rows/columns shelf)

- addFieldToRowsOrColumns takes `{field, shelfType}` where shelfType is "rows" or "columns". removeFieldFromRowsOrColumns takes `{field, shelfType, occurrence?}`. replaceFieldFromRowsOrColumns takes `{existingField, newField, shelfType, occurrence?}`.
- Examples:
  - "Add Category to rows": addFieldToRowsOrColumns `{field: {fieldName: "Category", objectName: "Orders"}, shelfType: "rows"}`
  - "Add total Sales to columns": addFieldToRowsOrColumns `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders", function: "Sum"}, shelfType: "columns"}`
  - "Add Order_Date to columns broken out by year": `{field: {fieldName: "Order_Date", objectName: "Orders", function: "DatePartYear"}, shelfType: "columns"}`
  - "Swap Category for Region on columns": replaceFieldFromRowsOrColumns `{existingField: {fieldName: "Category", objectName: "Orders"}, newField: {fieldName: "Region", objectName: "Orders"}, shelfType: "columns"}`

## Change field (rows/columns shelf)

- changeFieldOnRowsOrColumns changes an EXISTING shelf field's aggregation and/or display category, keeping it in place. Params: `{field, shelfType, occurrence?, function?, displayCategory?}` — supply at least one of `function` (an aggregation) or `displayCategory` ("Discrete" or "Continuous"); the omitted one is unchanged.
- Use for "average Sales instead of total", "aggregate Profit as a median", "make Sales discrete".
- Examples:
  - "average Sales instead of summing it" (Sales on columns): `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders", function: "Sum"}, shelfType: "columns", function: "Avg"}`
  - "make Sales on rows discrete": `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, shelfType: "rows", displayCategory: "Discrete"}`

## Label

- changeLabel renames the visualization: `{label: "Sales by Region"}`. (The name, not the title text drawn on the visualization.)

## Sort (rows/columns shelf)

- Sorts apply to a discrete field ALREADY on a shelf, identified by `targetField` `{fieldName, objectName?}`. Every copy on the shelf stays in sync.
- sortAscending / sortDescending sort by the field's OWN values (A→Z / Z→A).
- sortByField sorts `targetField` by the AGGREGATED value of `byField` `{fieldName, objectName?, function?}`. `byField.function` is the aggregation (default: measures keep their default, dimensions use "Count"; dimensions allow only Count/CountD/Min/Max). `descending` defaults true; set false for smallest first.
- clearSort removes the current sort.
- Examples:
  - "Sort Category A to Z": sortAscending `{targetField: {fieldName: "Category", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "Sort States by total Sales, largest first": sortByField `{targetField: {fieldName: "State", objectName: "Orders"}, byField: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders", function: "Sum"}}`
  - "Sort Category by count of Orders, smallest first": sortByField `{targetField: {fieldName: "Category", objectName: "Orders"}, byField: {fieldName: "Order_Id", objectName: "Orders", function: "Count"}, descending: false}`

## Mark encoding

- `encodingType` selects the slot and its rules:
  - Color — color by a field. One field; adding replaces the existing.
  - Label — annotate marks. Up to 3 fields; oldest dropped when full.
  - Tooltip — extra data on hover. Unlimited; must be a measure.
  - Size — size marks by a measure. One field; adding replaces the existing.
  - Detail — add granularity without changing other encodings. Unlimited.
- addFieldToEncoding / removeFieldFromEncoding take `{encodingType, field, targetField?}`; replaceFieldOnEncoding takes `{encodingType, existingField, newField, targetField?}`. `targetField` is optional, applies to all marks by default; set it to a field that already has its own mark (e.g. one measure of a multi-measure viz) to edit only that mark, else the operation errors.
- The special "Measure Names" field colors measures apart and has no name — reference it as `{field: {type: "MeasureNames"}}`, Color slot only (a dual axis adds it there).
- Examples:
  - "color the visualization by Region": addFieldToEncoding `{encodingType: "Color", field: {fieldName: "Region", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "stop coloring by Region": removeFieldFromEncoding `{encodingType: "Color", field: {fieldName: "Region", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "stop coloring the two measures apart" (remove the measure-names color a dual axis added): removeFieldFromEncoding `{encodingType: "Color", field: {type: "MeasureNames"}}`
  - "color by Region instead of by measure": replaceFieldOnEncoding `{encodingType: "Color", existingField: {type: "MeasureNames"}, newField: {fieldName: "Region", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "label the marks by Product": addFieldToEncoding `{encodingType: "Label", field: {fieldName: "Product", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "add Revenue to the tooltip": addFieldToEncoding `{encodingType: "Tooltip", field: {fieldName: "Revenue", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "size the bubbles by Sales": addFieldToEncoding `{encodingType: "Size", field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "break the marks down by Segment": addFieldToEncoding `{encodingType: "Detail", field: {fieldName: "Segment", objectName: "Orders"}}`

## Mark type

- changeMarkType sets the mark shape for the whole visualization, or one measure's mark. It changes shape only — it does not move fields, so it won't by itself convert a chart to one needing a different layout.
- `markType`: "Bar", "Line", "Circle", "Square", "Donut", "Text", or "automatic" (lets the viz pick). `targetField` (optional) retypes only one field's mark; that field must already be a mark.
- Examples: "draw the marks as lines" → `{markType: "Line"}`; "let the visualization choose" → `{markType: "automatic"}`.

## Dual axis

- A dual axis overlays two continuous fields (measures or dates, any combination) that are ALREADY adjacent on the SAME shelf. addDualAxis does not add fields — add the second with addFieldToRowsOrColumns first.
- `primaryField` is the LEFT field, `secondaryField` the RIGHT (their shelf order matters; the secondary moves onto the shared axis). Each is `{fieldName, objectName?, function?}`. Add `primaryOccurrence`/`secondaryOccurrence` (1-based) when name+object+function still repeat.
- `synchronization`: "None" (default; independent scales), "ZeroPosition" (zero lines align), or "FullRange" (shared range). Optional on addDualAxis; REQUIRED on synchronizeAxis. "ZeroPosition" is not allowed when both fields are dates of the same kind — use "FullRange" or "None".
- removeDualAxis and synchronizeAxis name the same (primary, secondary) pair.
- Examples:
  - "make Sales and Profit a dual axis" (both on columns, Sales left): addDualAxis `{primaryField: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, secondaryField: {fieldName: "Profit", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "overlay Profit on Sales with aligned zero lines": add `synchronization: "ZeroPosition"` to the above.
  - "make the Sales/Profit dual axis share one range": synchronizeAxis `{primaryField: {...Sales}, secondaryField: {...Profit}, synchronization: "FullRange"}`

## Reference line (VizQL visualizations only)

- A reference line marks a value on an axis `field` (`{fieldName, objectName?, function?}`) ALREADY on a shelf; these operations never add the field. When the same field is on the shelf under different aggregations, set `field.function` to pick the pill.
- Two different functions — do not confuse:
  - `field.function` selects the AXIS field (its shelf aggregation). "Sum of Sales" names THIS field.
  - `line.function` is the LINE's own computation (average line, max line). Set it only when the request names that statistic. So "add a reference line to Sum of Sales" attaches a default (average) line to the Sum-of-Sales pill — set `field.function: "Sum"` and OMIT `line`; it does NOT mean a sum line.
- Line kinds (`line`):
  - Computation line: `{valueType: "Computation", function}` where function is "Sum"/"Avg"/"Min"/"Max" (measure) or "Max"/"Min"/"Today"/"Now" (date). Omitting `line` on addReferenceLine defaults to an average line (measure) / latest-date line (date). To compute from a DIFFERENT field, set `line.computationField` `{fieldName, objectName?, function?}` (need not be on a shelf).
  - Constant line: `{valueType: "Value", value}` — a number (measure axis) or ISO date string (date axis).
- Optional label goes INSIDE `line`: `labelType` is "None"/"Value"/"Computation"/"Custom" (with `customLabel`). `scope` is "Table" (default)/"Pane"/"Cell". `lineColor` is a top-level hex (default gray), accepted by both add and edit.
- Selecting among multiple lines on a field: describe by `computationFunction`, `value`, `labelText`, `scope`, or `lineValueType`; or pick by position with `lineOccurrence` (1-based). `lineOccurrence` picks WHICH LINE; `occurrence` picks WHICH SHELF PILL (only when the field repeats on the shelf). When no pill is named, `lineOccurrence` counts across all matching pills.
- removeReferenceLine removes every matching line (all lines on the field unless narrowed by `scope`). editReferenceLine changes exactly ONE line (errors if ambiguous) and changes only what you pass: set `scope`/`lineColor`/`labelType`+`customLabel` to change just those (keeps the value); set `line` to change the value/function (keeps the label unless you also pass label fields).
- Examples:
  - "add an average line to Sales": addReferenceLine `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "add a target line at 5000 on Sales": `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, line: {valueType: "Value", value: 5000}}`
  - "add a line at 100 on avg of Sales labeled 'target' in green": `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders", function: "Avg"}, line: {valueType: "Value", value: 100, labelType: "Custom", customLabel: "target"}, lineColor: "#00FF00"}`
  - "add a sum line for Sales per pane": `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, line: {valueType: "Computation", function: "Sum"}, scope: "Pane"}`
  - "add an average line on Sales computed using sum of Discount": `{field: {...Sales}, line: {valueType: "Computation", function: "Avg", computationField: {fieldName: "Discount", objectName: "Orders", function: "Sum"}}}`
  - "add a max line on the 1st Sum of Sales" (repeated pill → occurrence): `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders", function: "Sum"}, occurrence: 1, line: {valueType: "Computation", function: "Max"}}`
  - "make the Sales reference line red" (color only, omit `line`): editReferenceLine `{field: {...Sales}, lineColor: "#FF0000"}`
  - "remove the 2nd reference line on avg of Sales": removeReferenceLine `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders", function: "Avg"}, lineOccurrence: 2}`
  - "update the 2nd reference line on the 1st Sum of Sales to a max line" (BOTH selectors): editReferenceLine `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders", function: "Sum"}, occurrence: 1, lineOccurrence: 2, line: {valueType: "Computation", function: "Max"}}`

## Table calculation (on a measure already on a shelf)

- Target a measure by `field` (`{fieldName, objectName?, function?}`, plus `occurrence` when it still repeats).
- `quickTableCalc.type`: RunningSum, RunningAvg, RunningMin, RunningMax, Difference, PercentDifference, PercentOfTotal, Rank, RankModified, RankDense, RankUnique, Percentile, MovingSum, MovingAverage, MovingMin, MovingMax.
  - Moving types accept `previousValues`, `nextValues`, `useCurrentValue`. MovingAverage defaults to 2/0/true; other moving types have no defaults.
  - Ranking types accept `order` ("Ascending"/"Descending"); Rank defaults "Descending".
- `computeUsing.type` (optional direction): TableAcross, TableDown, TableAcrossThenDown, TableDownThenAcross, PaneAcross, PaneDown, PaneAcrossThenDown, PaneDownThenAcross, Cell.
- applyTableCalc adds; editTableCalc changes (errors if none); removeTableCalc clears (errors if none).
- Examples:
  - "show Sales as a running total": applyTableCalc `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, quickTableCalc: {type: "RunningSum"}}`
  - "show a 3-period moving average of Sales": `{field: {...Sales}, quickTableCalc: {type: "MovingAverage", previousValues: 2, nextValues: 0, useCurrentValue: true}}`
  - "compute the running total down the table instead": editTableCalc `{field: {...Sales}, quickTableCalc: {type: "RunningSum"}, computeUsing: {type: "TableDown"}}`
  - "remove the table calculation from Sales": removeTableCalc `{field: {...Sales}}`

## Axis title

- editAxisTitle sets a custom axis label: `{field, axisTitle}`. resetAxisTitle reverts to default: `{field}`. Identify the axis by `field` (`fieldName`, `objectName`, optional `function`).
- Examples: "Rename the Y axis to Revenue" → editAxisTitle `{field: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, axisTitle: "Revenue"}`; "Reset the Revenue axis title" → resetAxisTitle `{field: {fieldName: "Revenue", objectName: "Orders"}}`.

## Forecast

- addForecast requires `measureField` `{fieldName, objectName?, function?}` and `dateDimensionField` `{fieldName, objectName?}`. Optional:
  - `forecastInterval` `{value, timeUnit}` where timeUnit is "Minutes"/"Hours"/"Days"/"Weeks"/"Months"/"Quarters"/"Years"; defaults to 4 periods at the date field's granularity.
  - `forecastModel`: "HoltWinters" (default) or "RidgeRegression".
  - `includeBounds`: true (default)/false. `confidenceLevel`: 90/95 (default)/99. `ignoreLastPeriods`: number. `fillNullsWithZero`: true/false (default). `granularity`: "InferFromData" (default; usually omit). `occurrence`: when the same measure appears more than once.
- editForecast updates an existing forecast (specify only what changes). removeForecast removes a specific forecast by `measureField`, or all forecasts when omitted. Forecasts require a time-series visualization (date on X, measure on Y).
- Examples:
  - "add a forecast for Sales": addForecast `{measureField: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, dateDimensionField: {fieldName: "OrderDate", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "forecast Sales for 6 months": add `forecastInterval: {value: 6, timeUnit: "Months"}`.
  - "forecast Revenue 12 months ahead using RidgeRegression": `{measureField: {fieldName: "Revenue"}, dateDimensionField: {fieldName: "Date"}, forecastInterval: {value: 12, timeUnit: "Months"}, forecastModel: "RidgeRegression"}`
  - "change the Sales forecast to 12 months": editForecast `{measureField: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}, forecastInterval: {value: 12, timeUnit: "Months"}}`
  - "remove all forecasts": removeForecast `{}`; "remove the Sales forecast": removeForecast `{measureField: {fieldName: "Sales", objectName: "Orders"}}`
  - "add a forecast to the second Sales": add `occurrence: 2`.

## Filters

**Field reference — model vs expression:**
- Use `{model: "Object.Field"}` for a simple comparison on the raw field value (no aggregation). e.g. "sales > 1000" → `{fields: [{model: "Orders.Sales"}], operator: "GreaterThan", values: [1000]}`.
- Use `{expression: "SUM(...)"}` etc. ONLY when the user names an aggregate ("total", "sum of", "average", "count of"), with `bucket: "aggregateFilter"`. A bare measure name with NO aggregate keyword is NOT an aggregate: "sales of at least 2000", "profit over 500", "quantity more than 10" all use `{model: "Object.Field"}`, never `SUM(...)`. Without an explicit aggregate keyword, ALWAYS use `{model: "Object.Field"}`.
- Use `{expression: "DATEPART(...)"}` for year/month/quarter/etc. filtering.
- Use a table-calc expression (RUNNING_SUM/RANK/WINDOW_*/...) with `bucket: "tableCalcFilter"`.
- Field references in expressions use bracket notation `[Object].[Field]`.

**Expression forms:**
- Date (DATEPART → integer, DATETRUNC → date): `DATEPART('year'|'quarter'|'month'|'week'|'day', [Object].[Field])`; `DATETRUNC('year'|'month'|'quarter', [Object].[Field])`.
- Aggregate (`bucket: "aggregateFilter"`): SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/COUNT/COUNTD/MEDIAN([Object].[Field]); ratios like `SUM([O].[Profit])/SUM([O].[Sales])`.
- Table calc (`bucket: "tableCalcFilter"`, always wrap an aggregate): RUNNING_SUM/RUNNING_AVG/RUNNING_MIN/RUNNING_MAX/RUNNING_COUNT(AGG(...)); RANK(AGG(...), 'ASC'|'DESC'); WINDOW_SUM/WINDOW_AVG(AGG(...), start, end).

**Operator rules:**
1. NEVER use Equals/DoesNotEquals — use In/NotIn ("Color is Red" → `operator: "In", values: ["Red"]`; supports multiple values).
2. ALWAYS use IgnoreCase string variants (ContainsIgnoreCase, StartsWithIgnoreCase, EndsWithIgnoreCase, DoesNotStartWithIgnoreCase, …) — users rarely mean case-sensitive.
3. NEVER put null/undefined in `values` — all values must be concrete. If you can't express both bounds concretely, choose another operator.

**Operators by category:**
- Equality (multi-value): In, NotIn.
- Comparison: Between, LessThan, LessThanOrEqualTo, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqualTo.
- String (IgnoreCase): ContainsIgnoreCase, NotContainsIgnoreCase, StartsWithIgnoreCase, DoesNotStartWithIgnoreCase, EndsWithIgnoreCase, DoesNotEndWithIgnoreCase.
- Null/Empty: IsNull, IsNotNull, IsEmpty, IsNotEmpty.
- Relative date (no values): CurrentDay/Week/Month/Quarter/Year, PreviousDay/Week/Month/Quarter/Year, NextDay/Week/Month/Quarter/Year.
- Relative date (`values: [N]`): LastNMinutes/Hours/Days/Weeks/Months/Quarters/Years, NextNDays/Weeks/Months/Quarters/Years.
- Fiscal (no values): CurrentFiscalWeek/Month/Quarter/Year. Fiscal (`values: [N]`): LastNFiscalWeeks/Months/Quarters/Years. Use fiscal ONLY when the user says "fiscal" — "this quarter" → CurrentQuarter, not CurrentFiscalQuarter.
- Date-to-date (uses `{model:...}`, no expression): CurrentYearToDate/MonthToDate/QuarterToDate/WeekToDate, PreviousYearToDate/MonthToDate/QuarterToDate/WeekToDate.
- TopN/BottomN: AdvancedDimension with `topBottomCriteria: {topBottomLimit, isTop, expression}` (isTop true for top N), `bucket: "advancedDimensionFilter"`.
- Relative-date form selection: "last/next <period>" (no number) → singular (PreviousWeek, NextMonth); "last/next N <periods>" → LastN/NextN; "last 1 quarter" → LastN form with `values: [1]`.

**Buckets (execution order):** filter (standard dimension), contextFilter (before aggregation), aggregateFilter (aggregated values), tableCalcFilter (table calcs), advancedDimensionFilter (TopN/BottomN).

**editFilter** updates an existing filter's expression; **removeFilter** removes it.

**Add-then-filter vs plain filter:**
- A query that only RESTRICTS data is ONE addFilter, even when it names a dimension: "filter to top 10 customers by sales" (TopN), "show orders from this year", "only show the West region". If the field is already on a shelf, just filter it.
- Add-then-filter applies ONLY when the user wants to SEE a dimension broken out by its values AND restrict which show, AND that dimension is not already on a shelf: FIRST addFieldToRowsOrColumns, THEN addFilter. e.g. "I want to see Region in East and West" (no Region on a shelf) → `[{addFieldToRowsOrColumns: {field: {fieldName: "Region", objectName: "Orders"}, shelfType: "rows"}}, {addFilter: {filter: {fields: [{model: "Orders.Region"}], operator: "In", values: ["East", "West"]}}}]`.
- Distinguish intent: FILTER/RESTRICT verbs ("filter to", "only show", "where", "restrict to") → addFilter; DISPLAY/ADD verbs ("add to rows", "put on columns", "place on shelf") → addFieldToRowsOrColumns. "show"/"display" + a condition usually means addFilter.

**Filter examples:**
- "sales greater than 1000" (raw field): `{filter: {fields: [{model: "Orders.Sales"}], operator: "GreaterThan", values: [1000]}}`
- "orders from 2020 and 2021": `{filter: {fields: [{expression: "DATEPART('year', [Orders].[Order_Date])"}], operator: "In", values: [2020, 2021]}}`
- "orders after June 2022" (DATETRUNC, ISO values): `{filter: {fields: [{expression: "DATETRUNC('month', [Orders].[Order_Date])"}], operator: "GreaterThan", values: ["2022-06-01"]}}`
- "where total sales > 10000" (aggregate): `{filter: {fields: [{expression: "SUM([Orders].[Sales])"}], operator: "GreaterThan", values: [10000]}, bucket: "aggregateFilter"}`
- "where profit margin > 15%": `{filter: {fields: [{expression: "SUM([Orders].[Profit])/SUM([Orders].[Sales])"}], operator: "GreaterThan", values: [0.15]}, bucket: "aggregateFilter"}`
- "where running sum of sales > 1000": `{filter: {fields: [{expression: "RUNNING_SUM(SUM([Orders].[Sales]))"}], operator: "GreaterThan", values: [1000]}, bucket: "tableCalcFilter"}`
- "top 10 states by sales": `{filter: {fields: [{model: "Orders.State"}], operator: "AdvancedDimension", topBottomCriteria: {topBottomLimit: 10, isTop: true, expression: "SUM([Orders].[Sales])"}}, bucket: "advancedDimensionFilter"}`

## Chaining Operations

`editOperations` is a JSON **string** encoding an array of `{operationType, params}` applied in order — each sees the previous one's result, all-or-nothing. Build the array, then JSON-serialize the whole thing into the string (never pass a raw array):

```json
[
  {"operationType": "addFieldToRowsOrColumns", "params": {"field": {"fieldName": "Category", "objectName": "Orders"}, "shelfType": "rows"}},
  {"operationType": "addFieldToRowsOrColumns", "params": {"field": {"fieldName": "Sales", "objectName": "Orders", "function": "Sum"}, "shelfType": "columns"}},
  {"operationType": "sortByField", "params": {"targetField": {"fieldName": "Category", "objectName": "Orders"}, "byField": {"fieldName": "Sales", "objectName": "Orders", "function": "Sum"}}}
]
```

Serialized into the full call payload (note the `inputs` wrapper and the escaped quotes inside `editOperations`):

```
{"inputs": [{"visualizationId": "<id>", "editOperations": "[{\"operationType\":\"changeMarkType\",\"params\":{\"markType\":\"Bar\"}}]"}]}
```

Each call returns the updated definition in `visualizationMetadata` and stores it under the same `visualizationId`; call again with that id to build a chart step by step. Each call renders inline, so no separate `render_visualization` is needed.

visualizationId.description: The id of the visualization to edit: the id returned by get_visualization, or by a previous edit_visualization or update_visualization.

editOperations.description: The ordered edit operations to apply, as a JSON array of {operationType, params} objects. Operations are applied in order as an all-or-nothing batch.

update_visualization.name: update_visualization
update_visualization.description:
Update an existing Tableau Next visualization in place. Call this ONLY when the
user EXPLICITLY asks to save, persist, re-save, or update the stored visualization
— it is NOT an automatic follow-up to `edit_visualization`, which intentionally
leaves its result unsaved. When invoked, it writes a visualization definition back
over the existing visualization via PATCH /tableau/visualizations/{id}.

The visualization to update is identified by `visualizationId`. The tool loads
that visualization's latest working definition by id — the baseline
`get_visualization` fetched, updated in place by any `edit_visualization` you ran
against the same id — so an edit followed by an update saves the edited state
without re-sending it.

Update is in place: it does NOT move the visualization to another workspace or
re-point it at a different semantic model. Both the workspace and the backing
semantic model are read from the loaded visualization definition itself (it
already carries them), so there is nothing else to pass.

**Inputs.** The argument goes inside a single-element `inputs` array — the call
payload is `{"inputs": [{"visualizationId": "<id>"}]}`, NOT the field at the top
level. The `inputs` array always has exactly one element.
- `visualizationId` (string, REQUIRED) — the `id` of the visualization to update:
  the `id` of one fetched with `get_visualization`, or the `id` returned by a
  previous `edit_visualization`/`update_visualization`.

**Returns:** a compact confirmation, NOT the visualization definition:
- `updateStatus` (string) — `SUCCESS` when the update was applied.

The saved visualization is the one you passed as `visualizationId`, so the id is
not echoed back. The saved definition is not returned either: update does not change
the visualization's metadata, so the working definition you already have (the one
`get_visualization` fetched and `edit_visualization` last modified) is still current.
Do not call `update_visualization` to read back the visualization — if you need its
current definition, use `get_visualization`, and to make further changes call
`edit_visualization` with the same `visualizationId`.

**Use when:** the user EXPLICITLY asks to save, persist, re-save, or update the
stored visualization (e.g. "save it", "persist my changes", "save the
visualization"). Editing a visualization does not on its own call for a save:
`edit_visualization` already renders its result inline, so after an edit, ask the
user whether they want to save the changes and call this tool only once they
confirm. This updates the visualization identified by `visualizationId` in place
rather than creating a copy.

visualizationId.description: The id of the visualization to update: the id returned by get_visualization, or by a previous edit_visualization or update_visualization.

list_workspaces.name: list_workspaces
list_workspaces.description:
Enumerate workspaces or fetch one by id when provided.

**Inputs:** optional `limit`, `offset`.

**Returns:** a single top-level key `workspaces[]` with `id`, `name`,
`label`, `description`, `createdBy` / `createdDate`, `lastModifiedBy` /
`lastModifiedDate`, `permissions` (`view` / `edit` / `share` /
`delete`), `url`.

**Use when:** you need containers and access context for assets.

**Caveats:**

- **No pagination metadata.** Unlike `list_semantic_models` (which
  returns `count`, `total`, `currentPageUrl`, `nextPageUrl`,
  `previousPageUrl`), this tool returns only the bare
  `{ "workspaces": [...] }` envelope. There is NO `total`, `hasMore`,
  `nextOffset`, or page URL. To detect "no more pages", page until you
  receive an empty array.

- **Sort order is undocumented oldest-first** (ascending by
  `createdDate`). To find the most recently created workspace, either
  page through everything and pick the last item, or use
  `browse_data_assets` with `AssetType: "AnalyticsWorkspace"` and
  `orderBy: "CreatedDate"` + `sortDirection: "Descending"` -- that
  endpoint exposes ordering and pagination metadata.

list_workspace_assets.name: list_workspace_assets
list_workspace_assets.description:
Enumerate assets contained in a specific workspace.

**Returns:** `workspaceAssets[]` with:
- `assetId`
- `assetType` (`AnalyticsDashboard` | `AnalyticsVisualization` |
  `SemanticModel`)
- `assetUsageType` (`Created` | `Referenced`)
- `createdBy` (id / name), `createdDate`
- `url`

**Use when:** you need dashboards, visualizations, and semantic models
scoped to a workspace. NOT for org-wide search across asset types --
use `browse_data_assets` for keyword discovery.

create_workspace.name: create_workspace
create_workspace.description:
Create a new Tableau Next workspace in the current org.

**Body inputs:**
- `name` (REQUIRED) -- developer / API identifier; alphanumeric +
  underscore, NO spaces, e.g. `Q3_Return_Insights`.
- `label` -- display name, free text, e.g. `Q3 Return Insights`.
- `description` (optional)

**Returns:** full workspace metadata including id, name, label,
permissions, url.

**Use when:** you need a new container for organizing dashboards,
visualizations, and semantic models.

**Caveats:**

- **Silent name transforms.** No warning, no `wasRenamed` flag, no
  `originalName` field, no error. The ONLY signal that your `name`
  was changed is the returned `name` differing from your input.
  Always read `name` back and string-compare against what you sent.
  - Duplicate `name` in the same org -> auto-renamed with a numeric
    suffix (`Foo` -> `Foo1` -> `Foo2`).
  - Non-ASCII / unicode characters -> silently stripped.
  - `name` longer than the max length -> silently truncated (observed
    cap around 80 characters).
  - Spaces in `name` -> silently converted to underscores. (This
    contradicts older guidance that spaces returned `JSON_PARSER_ERROR`;
    current behavior is a silent transform, not an error.)
  - Multiple transforms can stack in one call (e.g. spaces +
    duplicate -> rename to `My_Workspace1` in a single response).

- **Pre-flight check.** To detect a collision before calling, query
  `browse_data_assets` with:
  ```
  searchTerm: "<your-name>"
  filters: { filters: [
    { field: "AssetType", operator: "In",
      values: ["AnalyticsWorkspace"] }
  ]}
  ```
  Or page through `list_workspaces` (which returns oldest-first; you'll
  need to walk the full list since there's no pagination metadata).

- **Scope:** creates in current org only -- does NOT copy a workspace
  from another org.

- **Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
  `{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}`.
  Parse `JSON.parse(response.defaultExc)` to get the body.

name.description:
Developer / API identifier. Alphanumeric + underscore,
NO spaces (spaces are silently converted to underscores).
Duplicates auto-rename with a numeric suffix.

delete_workspace.name: delete_workspace
delete_workspace.description:
Delete a Tableau Next workspace permanently.

**Inputs:**
- `workspaceIdOrApiName` (path) -- the workspace's id or apiName from
  `list_workspaces`.

**Returns:** confirmation of deletion.

**Use when:** you need to remove a workspace from the current org.
DESTRUCTIVE -- there is no undo.

**Cascade behavior (DESTRUCTIVE):**

Deleting a workspace cascade-deletes every workspace-asset row whose
`assetUsageType=Created`, AND that delete propagates to the underlying
assets. Confirmed for:

- `AnalyticsVisualization` -- removed from `list_visualizations`
- `SemanticModel` -- removed from `list_semantic_models`
- `AnalyticsDashboard` -- removed from `list_dashboards`

Assets added with `assetUsageType=Referenced` are NOT deleted (only their
workspace association is removed).

**Side-effect interactions:**

- `create_dashboard` auto-creates a `Created` workspace-asset row for the
  new dashboard.
- `create_*_viz` likewise auto-creates a `Created` row for the new viz.

So any viz or dashboard authored in the workspace will be cascade-deleted
when the workspace is deleted. ALWAYS call `list_workspace_assets` first
to inventory `Created`-typed assets before deleting.

**Scope:** current org only.

**Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
`{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}`. Parse
`JSON.parse(response.defaultExc)` to get the body. EXCEPTION: on 204
success, `defaultExc` is the literal string `"204"` (NOT JSON-parseable).
Branch on `responseCode === 204` for the success path.

add_workspace_asset.name: add_workspace_asset
add_workspace_asset.description:
Add an existing asset (in this org) to a workspace.

**Calling convention.** This tool takes FLAT top-level args, NOT a body
wrapper. Passing `body={...}` returns a generic `UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION`.

**Inputs:**
- `workspaceIdOrApiName` (path)
- `assetId` -- SF id of an existing asset. Find candidates with
  `browse_data_assets` using `searchTerm: ""` and an `AssetType` filter,
  e.g. `MktDataLakeObject` for DLOs.
- `assetType` -- one of `AnalyticsDashboard`, `AnalyticsVisualization`,
  `SemanticModel`, `Flexipage`, `MktCalculatedInsightObject`,
  `MktDataConnection`, `MktDataLakeObject`, `MktDataModelObject`,
  `MktDataTransformSetup`.
- `assetUsageType` -- `Created` or `Referenced`. Pass `Referenced` to
  add a pointer to an asset created elsewhere; pass `Created` if the
  asset originated in this workspace.

**Returns:** workspace asset metadata with assetId, assetType,
assetUsageType, label, name, url.

**Use when:** you need to associate a dashboard, visualization, or
semantic model with a workspace.

**Caveats:**

- **Re-adds return 304 with no body.** Re-adding the same `assetId` +
  `workspaceIdOrApiName` returns HTTP 304 with no body. Even when the
  second call passes a DIFFERENT `assetUsageType`, the change is
  silently ignored -- there is no atomic "update usage type"
  operation. To change usage type, call `remove_workspace_asset` then
  `add_workspace_asset` again with the new value.

- **Scope:** associates assets that already exist in the current org;
  does NOT copy assets from another org.

- **Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
  `{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}`.
  Parse `JSON.parse(response.defaultExc)` to get the body.

assetType.description: Different types of asset that can be added to a workspace

assetUsageType.description: Different usage types of assets in a workspace

remove_workspace_asset.name: remove_workspace_asset
remove_workspace_asset.description:
Remove an asset reference from a workspace permanently.

**Inputs:**
- `workspaceIdOrApiName` (path) -- the workspace's id or apiName from
  `list_workspaces`.
- `assetId` (path) -- the SF id of the workspace asset row from
  `list_workspace_assets`.

**Returns:** confirmation of deletion.

**Use when:** you need to disassociate an asset (dashboard,
visualization, semantic model, etc.) from a workspace. DESTRUCTIVE --
there is no undo on the workspace association.

**Does NOT delete the underlying asset itself,** only the workspace
asset row that links it to this workspace; the asset remains in the
org and may still be referenced from other workspaces.

Counterpart to `add_workspace_asset`.

**Scope:** current org only.

**Caveats:**

- **Not idempotent.** A second call on the same asset returns
  `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (404) with `The specified asset doesn't exist`.
  Treat 404 on retry as success-equivalent if you may double-call.

- **Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
  `{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}`.
  Parse `JSON.parse(response.defaultExc)` to get the body. Note: 204
  No Content responses come back as `defaultExc: "204"` rather than a
  stringified JSON body.
