- **Cosmetic 404 message bug.** The 404 message currently substitutes
  the searched-for name into BOTH the entity slot AND the parent-model
  slot (e.g. `Semantic definition (X) doesn't exist in semantic model
  (X)` even when the model name is unrelated). Don't string-parse the
  message for the model name.

add_semantic_model_logical_view.name: add_semantic_model_logical_view
add_semantic_model_logical_view.description:
Add a new logical view on a semantic model.

A logical view is a virtual table layered on top of base data objects in an
SDM — a pre-joined, filtered, or union-shaped construct exposed to
visualizations without modifying the underlying data objects.

Use `get_semantic_model` to enumerate existing logical views
(`semanticLogicalViews[]`) before creating a new one.

# Required inputs

- `modelApiNameOrId` (path) — the SDM's `apiName` or `id`
- `apiName` — unique API name for the new logical view
- `label` — display name (required; server rejects without it)

# Type quick-reference

| `semanticViewTypeEnum` | What it does | Key field | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HardJoin` | Pre-computed join of multiple data objects | `semanticDataObjects[]` | Medium — add relationships in a second call |
| *(omit for Union)* | Unions same-shaped tables into one virtual table | `semanticUnions[]` | High — mapped-field alignment required; **do NOT pass `"Union"`** |
| `CustomSQL` | Raw SQL expression with explicit field definitions | `customSQLV2` + one `semanticDataObjects` entry | Medium — explicit fields required |
| `Hierarchy` | DC hierarchy LV — **not currently supported via MCP** | — | — |

# HardJoin

Pre-computes a join of multiple data objects. Relationships must be added
after creation because the server assigns semantic field apiNames
(e.g. `LV_Orders_Id__c_1`) at first save time — those names are not
known in advance.

**Pattern:**
1. Call `add_semantic_model_logical_view` with `semanticDataObjects` only (no `semanticRelationships`).
2. Call `get_semantic_model_logical_view` to read the assigned field apiNames.
3. Call `add_semantic_model_relationship` with the correct field apiNames.

**Rules:**
- `dataObjectName` must include the type suffix: `__dll` (DLO), `__dlm` (DMO), `__dlc` (CIO).
- Each `semanticDataObjects` entry must have a unique `apiName` distinct from any existing model-level data object apiName — reusing one causes a "Unique constraint violated" error.
- When `shouldIncludeAllFields: true`, numeric suffixes are appended to every field apiName at save time; always read back to learn the actual names before adding relationships.
- Use `joinType` values `Left`/`Right`/`Inner`/`Full` for logical-view relationships (not `Auto`, which is for model-level relationships).

**Example — two-table HardJoin (step 1 of 3):**

```json
{
  "modelApiNameOrId": "SalesSDM",
  "apiName": "OrdersWithCustomers_LV",
  "label": "Orders with Customers",
  "semanticViewTypeEnum": "HardJoin",
  "semanticDataObjects": [
    {
      "apiName": "LV_Orders",
      "label": "Orders",
      "dataObjectName": "orders__dll",
      "dataObjectType": "Dlo",
      "shouldIncludeAllFields": true
    },
    {
      "apiName": "LV_Customers",
      "label": "Customers",
      "dataObjectName": "customers__dll",
      "dataObjectType": "Dlo",
      "shouldIncludeAllFields": true
    }
  ]
}
```

After step 1, call `get_semantic_model_logical_view` to learn the
server-assigned field apiNames, then `add_semantic_model_relationship`
to wire the join.

# Union

Unions same-shaped tables into a single virtual table. All tables live
inside **exactly one** `semanticUnions[]` entry — do not create one ULV
entry per table.

**Rules:**
- Use `semanticUnions[]`, NOT top-level `semanticDataObjects[]`.
- `semanticUnions` must contain exactly one entry; that entry holds all
  tables being unioned in its own `semanticDataObjects[]`.
- `semanticMappedFields[]` has one entry per unified output column; each
  entry's `fields[]` has one reference per data object
  (`tableApiName` + `fieldApiName`).
- **`fieldApiName` in `fields[]` must be the semantic dimension or
  measurement `apiName` as defined in the data object's
  `semanticDimensions[]` / `semanticMeasurements[]` — NOT the raw
  underlying `dataObjectFieldName` (e.g. `order_id__c`) and NOT the
  base model's server-assigned semantic field apiNames (e.g. `Order_Id8`
  from `get_semantic_model`). Both fail with "Field API name X not found
  in either measurements or dimensions."** Define explicit
  `semanticDimensions` and `semanticMeasurements` on each ULV data
  object and reference those locally-scoped apiNames in `fields[]`.
- All `semanticMappedFields.apiName` values must be globally unique.
- Each `semanticDimension` / `semanticMeasurement` inside a mapped field
  must be **fully populated** (`apiName`, `label`, `dataObjectFieldName`,
  `dataType`) — a partial object causes a 500 on read-back.
- Set `scanMinimalTables: true` on the ULV entry when the parent LV is
  used in a shared-dimension merge model.

**Example — two-table Union:**

> **WARNING:** Do NOT include `"semanticViewTypeEnum": "Union"` in the
> request body. The server infers Union type from the presence of
> `semanticUnions[]` and returns a 500 error if `semanticViewTypeEnum`
> is explicitly set to `"Union"`. Omit the field entirely.
>
> **Known server bug:** Union views are returned with
> `semanticViewTypeEnum: "HardJoin"` in GET responses. This is a
> cosmetic server-side misclassification — the view is stored correctly
> and functions as a Union.

```json
{
  "modelApiNameOrId": "SalesSDM",
  "apiName": "AllOrders_LV",
  "label": "All Orders",
  "semanticUnions": [
    {
      "apiName": "AllOrders_ULV",
      "label": "All Orders ULV",
      "semanticDataObjects": [
        {
          "apiName": "LV_Orders_US",
          "label": "Orders US",
          "dataObjectName": "orders_us__dll",
          "dataObjectType": "Dlo",
          "semanticDimensions": [
            {
              "apiName": "US_OrderId",
              "label": "Order ID",
              "dataObjectFieldName": "order_id__c",
              "dataType": "Text"
            }
          ],
          "semanticMeasurements": [
            {
              "apiName": "US_Revenue",
              "label": "Revenue",
              "dataObjectFieldName": "revenue__c",
              "dataType": "Currency",
              "aggregationType": "Sum"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "apiName": "LV_Orders_EU",
          "label": "Orders EU",
          "dataObjectName": "orders_eu__dll",
          "dataObjectType": "Dlo",
          "semanticDimensions": [
            {
              "apiName": "EU_OrderId",
              "label": "Order ID",
              "dataObjectFieldName": "order_id__c",
              "dataType": "Text"
            }
          ],
          "semanticMeasurements": [
            {
              "apiName": "EU_Revenue",
              "label": "Revenue",
              "dataObjectFieldName": "revenue__c",
              "dataType": "Currency",
              "aggregationType": "Sum"
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "semanticMappedFields": [
        {
          "apiName": "MF_OrderId",
          "label": "Order ID",
          "fields": [
            {"tableApiName": "LV_Orders_US", "fieldApiName": "US_OrderId"},
            {"tableApiName": "LV_Orders_EU", "fieldApiName": "EU_OrderId"}
          ],
          "semanticDimension": {
            "apiName": "MF_OrderId_dim",
            "label": "Order ID",
            "dataObjectFieldName": "order_id__c",
            "dataType": "Text"
          }
        },
        {
          "apiName": "MF_Revenue",
          "label": "Revenue",
          "fields": [
            {"tableApiName": "LV_Orders_US", "fieldApiName": "US_Revenue"},
            {"tableApiName": "LV_Orders_EU", "fieldApiName": "EU_Revenue"}
          ],
          "semanticMeasurement": {
            "apiName": "MF_Revenue_meas",
            "label": "Revenue",
            "dataObjectFieldName": "revenue__c",
            "dataType": "Currency",
            "aggregationType": "Sum"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

# CustomSQL

A logical view backed by a raw SQL expression. The data object describes
the output columns of the SQL.

**Rules:**
- `customSQLV2` carries the SQL expression (prefer over legacy `customSQL`).
- `semanticDataObjects` must contain **exactly one** entry with
  `dataObjectType: "CustomSQL"`.
- That entry must have at least one explicit `semanticDimensions[]` or
  `semanticMeasurements[]` entry — `shouldIncludeAllFields: true` does
  NOT satisfy this validation for CustomSQL data objects.
- Dimension fields require: `apiName`, `label`, `dataObjectFieldName`, `dataType`.
- Measurement fields additionally require: `aggregationType`.

**Example:**

```json
{
  "modelApiNameOrId": "SalesSDM",
  "apiName": "TopCustomers_LV",
  "label": "Top Customers",
  "semanticViewTypeEnum": "CustomSQL",
  "customSQLV2": "SELECT customer_id__c, customer_name__c, SUM(revenue__c) AS total_revenue__c FROM orders__dll GROUP BY customer_id__c, customer_name__c",
  "semanticDataObjects": [
    {
      "apiName": "LV_TopCustomers_SQL",
      "label": "Top Customers SQL",
      "dataObjectName": "orders__dll",
      "dataObjectType": "CustomSQL",
      "semanticDimensions": [
        {
          "apiName": "CustomerId_dim",
          "label": "Customer ID",
          "dataObjectFieldName": "customer_id__c",
          "dataType": "Text"
        },
        {
          "apiName": "CustomerName_dim",
          "label": "Customer Name",
          "dataObjectFieldName": "customer_name__c",
          "dataType": "Text"
        }
      ],
      "semanticMeasurements": [
        {
          "apiName": "TotalRevenue_meas",
          "label": "Total Revenue",
          "dataObjectFieldName": "total_revenue__c",
          "dataType": "Currency",
          "aggregationType": "Sum"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

# Common fields (all types)

- `tableType` — `Standard` or `Shared`
- `primaryNameField` — apiName of the field to use as the primary display name
- `semanticOverridePolicyType` — `Add`, `Merge`, or `Replace`
- `autoCreateRowCountSystemCalc` — when `true`, auto-creates a system-managed row-count measure
- `filterLogic` / `filters[]` — row-level filters; `filterLogic` (e.g. `"1 AND 2"`) required when `filters` has more than one entry; `filters[].fieldName` must be fully qualified as `<dataObjectApiName>.<fieldApiName>`

# Returns

The created logical view representation including `id`, `apiName`,
`semanticViewTypeEnum`, and the resolved data objects and relationships.

# Common errors

- `Unique constraint violated` — a `semanticDataObjects` entry reuses an
  apiName that already exists as a model-level data object. Use a distinct
  apiName prefixed with `LV_`.
- `Required fields are missing: [MasterLabel]` (500 on read-back) — a
  `semanticDimension` / `semanticMeasurement` inside a Union mapped field
  was only partially populated. All four required fields must be present.
- Server validation error on CustomSQL — either zero or more than one entry
  in `semanticDataObjects`, or the single entry has no explicit fields.
- Relationship criteria referencing wrong field names — use
  `get_semantic_model_logical_view` after creation to read server-assigned
  field apiNames before calling `add_semantic_model_relationship`.

apiName.description: Unique API name for this logical view on the SDM.

label.description: Display name. REQUIRED — server rejects without it.

semanticViewTypeEnum.description:
The join strategy for this logical view.
- `HardJoin` — pre-computed join of multiple data objects.
  Add relationships via `add_semantic_model_relationship`
  AFTER creating the view (field apiNames not available until
  after first save — see criteria caveat below).
- `Union` — parent container for unioned tables. Use the
  `semanticUnions` field (NOT `semanticDataObjects`) to
  supply the unioned tables. Each ULV entry in
  `semanticUnions` holds its own `semanticDataObjects` and
  `semanticMappedFields` for column alignment.
  **DO NOT pass `semanticViewTypeEnum: "Union"` in the
  request body** — the server infers Union type from the
  presence of `semanticUnions[]` and returns a 500 error
  if the field is explicitly set to "Union".
- `CustomSQL` — raw SQL expression; pair with `customSQLV2`.
  Requires exactly one `semanticDataObjects` entry with
  `dataObjectType: "CustomSQL"` and at least one field.
  Also requires `referenceIntegritySemanticDataObjects` containing
  the underlying DMO(s) referenced in the SQL, with all fields
  used in the SQL explicitly listed — `shouldIncludeAllFields: true`
  is silently ignored on reference objects and will cause a
  "Field X is not exist in reference data objects" error.

customSQL.description:
Legacy custom SQL expression (v1). Prefer `customSQLV2`.
Only relevant when `semanticViewTypeEnum` is `CustomSQL`.

customSQLV2.description:
Custom SQL expression (v2). Only relevant when
`semanticViewTypeEnum` is `CustomSQL`.

primaryNameField.description: API name of the field to use as the primary display name.

semanticOverridePolicyType.description:
How override properties are applied when this view is
layered on top of base data objects.

autoCreateRowCountSystemCalc.description:
When true, auto-creates a system-managed row-count calculated
measure on the logical view.

filterLogic.description:
Boolean filter-logic string, e.g. "1" or "1 AND 2".
Required when `filters` has more than one entry.

semanticDataObjects.description:
Data objects to include in this logical view. Each item
uses the same shape as `add_semantic_model_data_object`.
Inlined (not $ref) to avoid the OASToMCPConverter
circular-reference issue.

dataObjectName.description:
Underlying DLO/DMO/CIO API name with the type suffix:
`__dll` for DLOs, `__dlm` for DMOs, `__dlc` for CIOs.
e.g. `pr_metrics__dll`. Bare names are rejected.

shouldIncludeAllFields.description:
When true, all fields auto-attach as dimensions / measures.
Triggers numeric-suffix mutation on every apiName.

semanticDimensions.description:
Explicit dimension fields on this data object. Required
when `dataObjectType` is `CustomSQL` and
`shouldIncludeAllFields` is false or absent — the server
rejects CustomSQL data objects with no fields.
Each entry maps one output column to a semantic dimension.

semanticMeasurements.description:
Explicit measurement fields on this data object. Use
alongside `semanticDimensions` for CustomSQL data objects
that expose numeric aggregateable columns.

semanticUnions.description:
Required for Union-type logical views. Contains exactly one
ULV entry. That single entry holds ALL tables being unioned
inside its `semanticDataObjects[]` — do NOT create one ULV
per table. `semanticMappedFields` maps columns across the
unioned tables: one entry per unified output field, with
`fields[]` containing one reference per table. All
`semanticMappedFields.apiName` values must be globally
unique. `scanMinimalTables: true` is required on the ULV
when the parent is a shared-dimension merge model.

CRITICAL — union field mapping pattern:
1. Set `shouldIncludeAllFields: false` on each union data object.
2. Explicitly define `semanticDimensions` and/or
   `semanticMeasurements` on each data object in
   `semanticDataObjects[]`, giving each field a locally-scoped
   `apiName` (e.g. `p1_product_name`, `p2_product_name`).
3. In `semanticMappedFields[].fields[]`, set `fieldApiName` to
   these locally-defined names — NOT the base model's semantic
   field apiNames (e.g. `Product_Name8`) or raw column names
   (e.g. `product_name__c`). Both fail with:
   "Field API name X not found in either measurements or dimensions."

scanMinimalTables.description:
Set to true when the parent LV is used in a
shared-dimension merge model.

semanticDataObjects.description:
Data objects to include in this ULV. Same shape as
the top-level `semanticDataObjects`. Each entry must
have a unique `apiName`. Set `shouldIncludeAllFields:
false` and explicitly list fields via
`semanticDimensions` / `semanticMeasurements` — the
locally-defined `apiName` values on those entries are
what `semanticMappedFields[].fields[].fieldApiName`
must reference.

dataObjectName.description:
Underlying DLO/DMO apiName with type suffix
(`__dll`, `__dlm`, `__dlc`).

semanticDimensions.description:
REQUIRED for union data objects when
`shouldIncludeAllFields: false`. Explicitly define
each dimension field with a locally-scoped `apiName`
(e.g. `p1_product_name`). The `fieldApiName` values
in `semanticMappedFields[].fields[]` MUST reference
these locally-defined names — NOT the base model's
semantic field apiNames or raw column names (e.g.
`product_name__c` or `Product_Name8` both fail).

semanticMeasurements.description:
REQUIRED for union data objects when
`shouldIncludeAllFields: false`. Explicitly define
each measurement field with a locally-scoped `apiName`
(e.g. `p1_unit_price`). The `fieldApiName` values
in `semanticMappedFields[].fields[]` MUST reference
these locally-defined names.

semanticMappedFields.description:
Column-alignment entries: one per unified output field.
Each entry maps corresponding columns from each data
object into a single output field. Exactly one of
`semanticDimension` or `semanticMeasurement` must be
set (not both).

fields.description:
One entry per data object being unioned.
`tableApiName` is the data object's `apiName`;
`fieldApiName` MUST be the locally-scoped apiName
defined in that data object's `semanticDimensions`
or `semanticMeasurements` — NOT a raw column name
(e.g. `product_name__c`) or a base model semantic
field name (e.g. `Product_Name8`).

semanticDimension.description:
Set this OR semanticMeasurement, not both.
Must be fully populated — the server persists
this as a dimension entity and requires all
fields; a partial object causes a
`Required fields are missing: [MasterLabel]`
500 on read-back.

semanticMeasurement.description:
Set this OR semanticDimension, not both.
Must be fully populated — same reason as
semanticDimension above.

referenceIntegritySemanticDataObjects.description:
Data objects included for reference integrity purposes only —
they are not part of the join graph but are required to resolve
foreign-key references within the view.

**REQUIRED for `CustomSQL` logical views.** Every DMO/DLO
referenced in the SQL must appear here with ALL fields used in
the SQL explicitly listed in `semanticDimensions` and
`semanticMeasurements`. `shouldIncludeAllFields: true` is
silently ignored on reference objects — the server will reject
with "Field X is not exist in reference data objects" if any
SQL column is missing from the explicit field lists.

dataObjectName.description:
Underlying DLO/DMO apiName with type suffix
(`__dll`, `__dlm`, `__dlc`).

shouldIncludeAllFields.description:
WARNING: silently ignored on reference integrity objects.
Always explicitly list fields in `semanticDimensions` and
`semanticMeasurements` instead.

semanticDimensions.description:
Explicit dimension fields. Required for CustomSQL logical
views — list every dimension column referenced in the SQL.

semanticMeasurements.description:
Explicit measurement fields. Required for CustomSQL logical
views — list every numeric column referenced in the SQL.

semanticRelationships.description:
Relationships (joins) between data objects scoped to this
logical view. Each item uses the same shape as
`add_semantic_model_relationship`. Inlined to avoid the
OASToMCPConverter circular-reference issue.

leftSemanticDefinitionApiName.description: apiName of the left data object in the join.

rightSemanticDefinitionApiName.description: apiName of the right data object in the join.

joinType.description:
Use `Left`, `Right`, `Inner`, or `Full` for logical-view
scoped relationships. `Auto` is for model-level relationships.

criteria.description:
Join criteria. Typically one Equals criterion on a key column.
IMPORTANT: `leftSemanticFieldApiName` / `rightSemanticFieldApiName`
must be the server-assigned semantic field apiNames (e.g.
`LV_MyObject_Id__c_1`), NOT raw underlying column names. These
names are only known after the view is first saved. To set join
criteria: (1) create the view without `semanticRelationships`,
(2) call `get_semantic_model_logical_view` to learn field
apiNames, (3) call `add_semantic_model_relationship`.

update_semantic_model_logical_view.name: update_semantic_model_logical_view
update_semantic_model_logical_view.description:
Update entity-level properties of a logical view on a semantic model (PATCH semantics).

Only the fields you supply are updated; omitted fields are left unchanged.
This operation does NOT affect child data objects or relationships scoped to
the view — use `add_semantic_model_data_object` and
`add_semantic_model_relationship` to manage those.

**Required inputs:**
- `modelApiNameOrId` (path) — the SDM's apiName or id
- `logicalViewApiNameOrId` (path) — the logical view's apiName or id
- At least one body field — an empty body `{}` is rejected

**Updatable fields:**
- `description`
- `filterLogic` / `filters[]` — replace the view's row-level filters

**Fields that CANNOT be updated after creation:**
The server only persists `description`, `filterLogic`, and `filters` on PATCH.
All other fields — `semanticViewTypeEnum`, `customSQL`/`customSQLV2`,
`tableType`, `primaryNameField`, `semanticOverridePolicyType`,
`autoCreateRowCountSystemCalc` — are silently discarded. If the user asks to
change the SQL query or view type, inform them this is not supported via PATCH
and they must delete and recreate the logical view with the new SQL.

**Label rename is not supported via PATCH:**
The `label` field is intentionally absent from this tool. The underlying API
accepts `label` without error but silently ignores it — the value is never
persisted. If the user asks to rename a logical view, inform them that label
rename via PATCH is not currently supported by the API.

**Returns:** the updated logical view representation.

**Use `get_semantic_model_logical_view` first** to read the current state
before issuing a partial update, so you don't accidentally overwrite
filters or SQL you didn't intend to change.

logicalViewApiNameOrId.description: The logical view's apiName or id.

filterLogic.description: Boolean filter-logic string, e.g. "1" or "1 AND 2".

delete_semantic_model_logical_view.name: delete_semantic_model_logical_view
delete_semantic_model_logical_view.description:
Delete a logical view from a semantic model.

**Required inputs:**
- `modelApiNameOrId` (path) — the SDM's apiName or id
- `logicalViewApiNameOrId` (path) — the logical view's apiName or id

**Optional inputs:**
- `relationshipCascadeDelete` (query, boolean) — when `true`, also deletes
  any relationship dependencies on this logical view. Defaults to `false`;
  omitting it leaves orphaned relationships intact, which may cause errors
  on subsequent queries.

**Returns:** empty body on success (HTTP 204).

**Caveats:**
- This is irreversible. Confirm the target apiName with
  `get_semantic_model_logical_view` before deleting.
- If the logical view is referenced by other definitions (calc fields,
  metrics, dimensions/measures defined on it, other logical views),
  deleting it is BLOCKED until those dependents are removed or repointed.
  **Pre-flight first:** call `list_semantic_model_dependencies` **with
  `rawEdges=true`** and check whether any entry's `dependencies[]`
  references this logical view's apiName (or the apiName of a data object
  the view owns). (`rawEdges=true` is required: the default mode collapses
  definition-on-definition edges. `get_semantic_model_logical_view` also
  surfaces a `dependencies` list.)
- **Blocked-delete error shape differs from the other delete tools.**
  Unlike the calc-field / metric deletes -- which return a clean
  "can't be deleted because it has dependent elements" message that names
  each dependent -- a blocked logical-view delete currently surfaces as an
  **HTTP 500 with a raw Java stack trace** whose root cause contains
  `VetoDataChangeException ... DEPENDENCY_EXISTS` (message: "This semantic
  definition is referenced elsewhere in Salesforce. Remove the usage and
  try again."). Treat a 500 containing `DEPENDENCY_EXISTS` as a
  **dependency block, NOT a transient/internal failure** -- do not retry
  it. The stack trace does **not** name the blocking dependent; identify it
  from the `list_semantic_model_dependencies` (`rawEdges=true`) pre-flight
  or `get_semantic_model_logical_view`'s `dependencies` list.
- `relationshipCascadeDelete: true` clears only dependent **relationship
  rows** -- it does NOT clear calc-field / metric / dimension dependents
  defined on the view, so those will still block the delete. Set it `true`
  unless you have a specific reason to preserve orphaned relationships, but
  clear non-relationship dependents manually first.

relationshipCascadeDelete.description: A flag to indicate whether to delete relationship dependencies or not, the default is false.

list_semantic_model_parameters.name: list_semantic_model_parameters
list_semantic_model_parameters.description:
Enumerate parameters (dynamic filter/range inputs) defined on a semantic model.

**Inputs:**
- `modelApiNameOrId` (path)

**Returns:** collection of parameter metadata for the given semantic model.

**Use when:** you need to enumerate the dynamic filter/range inputs available
on a semantic model — for example before referencing a parameter in a
visualization or metric filter.

**Scope:** current org only.

add_semantic_model_parameter.name: add_semantic_model_parameter
add_semantic_model_parameter.description:
Add a parameter (dynamic filter input) to a semantic model.

**Inputs:**
- `modelApiNameOrId` (path)
- `apiName`, `label`, `type` (`All` or `List`), `dataType`
- `defaultValue` — required for all parameter types
- for `List` type: `values` (array of plain strings; `defaultValue` must match one)
- optional: `description`

**Returns:** created parameter metadata.

**Use when:** you need to add a user-controllable filter input to a semantic
model. Parameters are model-scoped (not tied to a specific data object). Use
`List` to constrain to a fixed set of values, or `All` to allow any value of
the given data type.

**Scope:** current org only.

type.description: The parameter type. Use `List` to constrain to an explicit set of allowed values; `All` to allow any value.

defaultValue.description: The default value of the parameter. Required for all parameter types. For `List` type, must exactly match one of the strings in `values`.

values.description: Allowed values for a `List` parameter. Each entry is a plain string — display names are auto-generated from the value. Required when type is `List`; ignored otherwise. The `defaultValue` must exactly match one of these strings.

update_semantic_model_parameter.name: update_semantic_model_parameter
update_semantic_model_parameter.description:
Update a parameter on a semantic model.

**This tool is PUT-style, not PATCH — full payload required on every call.**

You MUST re-send `label`, `type`, `dataType`, and `defaultValue` on every
call, even if only changing `description`. The server will reject incomplete
bodies with a validation error.

`apiName` is immutable — omit it from the body. Passing a different `apiName`
is silently ignored.

**Inputs:**
- `modelApiNameOrId` (path)
- `parameterApiNameOrId` (path) — the `apiName` or Salesforce ID of the parameter
- `label` — required
- `type` — required; `All` or `List`
- `dataType` — required; one of `Boolean`, `Date`, `DateTime`, `Email`, `Number`, `Percentage`, `PhoneNumber`, `Text`, `Url`
- `defaultValue` — required; for `List` type must exactly match one entry in `values`
- `description` — optional
- `values` — required when `type` is `List`; array of plain strings; `defaultValue` must match one

**Returns:** updated parameter metadata.

**Use when:** you need to change a parameter's label, allowed values, default,
or data type.

**Scope:** current org only.

**Response shape caveat:** this tool double-wraps as
`{"defaultExc": "<stringified JSON>", "responseCode": <number>}` at the API
level, but the MCP tool unwraps transparently — callers receive the parsed
parameter object directly.

type.description: The parameter type. Use `List` to constrain to an explicit set of allowed values; `All` to allow any value.

defaultValue.description: The default value of the parameter. For `List` type, must exactly match one of the strings in `values`.

values.description: Allowed values for a `List` parameter. Each entry is a plain string. Required when type is `List`; ignored otherwise. The `defaultValue` must exactly match one of these strings.

add_widget_to_dashboard.name: add_widget_to_dashboard
add_widget_to_dashboard.description:
Add a widget to a dashboard and place it on the grid in one atomic
operation. Handles the read-modify-write internally -- you do NOT need
to call `get_dashboard` or `update_dashboard` separately.

**Inputs:**
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (REQUIRED) -- dashboard id or apiName.
- `widget` (REQUIRED) -- `{ type, name, source?, textContent? }`:
  - `type` must be lowercase: `"visualization"`, `"text"`, `"filter"`,
    `"image"`, `"metric"`, `"navigation"`.
  - `name` is the unique key within the dashboard.
  - `source` is `{ id, name }` only -- do NOT include `source.label` or
    `source.type`.
  - For `type: "text"`, set `textContent` to populate the text widget. The
    tool converts the plain string into the dashboard's Quill Delta format and
    persists a left-aligned trailing newline. Omit it only when you explicitly
    want a blank text widget.
- `placement` (REQUIRED) -- `{ row, column, rowspan, colspan,
  pageIndex? }`. `pageIndex` defaults to 0.

**Returns:** `dashboardId`, `dashboardName`, `widgetName`.

**Grid defaults:** 48 columns, 20px row height, 1200px max width.
Common sizes: full-width = `colspan: 48`, half-width = `colspan: 24`,
standard height = `rowspan: 20`.

**Text widget example:**
```json
{
  "type": "text",
  "name": "text_0",
  "textContent": "Q4 Summary"
}
```

**Use when:** adding a viz, text block, filter, image, or metric
widget to an existing dashboard.

**Do NOT use when:**
- creating a dashboard from scratch -> `create_dashboard`
- rearranging existing widgets -> `update_dashboard`

**Caveats:**

- **`metric` widget shape.** Metric widgets need three pieces:
  - `widget.source.name` (REQUIRED) -- the saved metric's apiName
    (e.g. `"My_Metric"`). The persisted widget stores apiName only; an
    `id` alone won't render. Use `list_semantic_model_metrics` on the
    SDM to discover valid apiNames. (You may also pass `source.id` as
    a hint, but it's not what the renderer resolves on.)
  - `widget.semanticModelIdOrName` (REQUIRED) -- the SDM id
    (`2SMxx...`) or apiName the saved metric belongs to. The server
    populates `parameters.metricOption.sdmId / sdmApiName` from this,
    which the dashboard PATCH receiver requires (omitting it NPEs
    server-side).
  - `widget.type: "metric"`.
  Raw-measure refs, calculated-measure refs, and SDM apiNames-as-source
  are NOT accepted. Omitting `source.name` or `semanticModelIdOrName`
  returns a clear `INVALID_INPUT` error.

- **`navigation` widget shape.** Navigation widgets need:
  - `widget.navigationTargetPages` (REQUIRED) -- array of dashboard
    page names (matching `layouts[0].pages[].name` in the dashboard)
    in display order. Each page becomes one navigation item. Those
    target pages must actually HAVE those `name`s set -- `create_dashboard`
    bulk-create does NOT auto-derive `page_N`, so a nav item pointing at
    an unnamed page will not resolve. Name every page on create (or via
    `add_dashboard_page`) before wiring navigation to it.
  - `widget.navigationLabel` (OPTIONAL) -- display label for the
    navigation widget. Sets the widget's top-level `label` (persisted
    as the dashboard widget's Label field). Omit to leave it unset.
  - `widget.type: "navigation"`.
  The server populates `parameters.navigationItems` with one item per
  page (`type="page"`, `target=<pageName>`, `order=<index>`).
  Omitting `navigationTargetPages` returns `INVALID_INPUT`.

  A navigation widget belongs on EVERY page, so call this tool once per
  page (varying only `placement.pageIndex`) with the SAME widget `name`
  and the SAME definition each time. Re-using a widget `name` is allowed
  by IDENTITY: an identical definition reuses the stored widget and just
  adds the new page placement; a DIFFERENT definition under the same
  `name` is rejected (widget-already-exists). So keep
  `navigationTargetPages` / `navigationLabel` identical across the calls.

- **Opaque errors.** Almost every input mistake (missing required
  fields, wrong source shape, nonexistent ids, type/case mismatches)
  collapses to `UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION` with only an opaque ErrorId. The
  one exception is `visualization` widgets, which give clearer errors
  for unknown viz ids. Validate inputs before calling.

placement.description: Grid placement for a widget on a dashboard page.

colspan.description: Width in grid columns (e.g. 24 for half-width, 48 for full-width).

pageIndex.description:
0-based index of the page within layouts[0].pages[]. Defaults
to 0 (first page). If the page does not exist, returns an error.

rowspan.description: Height in grid rows (e.g. 20 for a standard tile).

widget.description: A dashboard widget definition. The "type" field determines the widget kind.

name.description:
Unique widget name within the dashboard. Used as the key in
the widgets map and referenced in layout placements. Must be
unique across all widgets in this dashboard.

navigationLabel.description:
Optional display label for the navigation widget. Ignored for
non-navigation widget types.

navigationTargetPages.description:
REQUIRED for type="navigation": the dashboard pages this
navigation widget links to, in display order. Each entry is a
page name (matching a page in layouts[0].pages[].name).
Ignored for non-navigation widget types. The server uses this
to populate the navigation widget's parameters.

semanticModelIdOrName.description:
REQUIRED for type="metric": the Semantic Model the saved
metric belongs to. Pass the SDM "id" (e.g. "2SMxx...") or
its developer "apiName". Ignored for non-metric widget
types. The server uses this to populate the metric widget's
parameters.metricOption.sdmId / sdmApiName, which the
dashboard PATCH receiver requires for metric widgets.

source.description: Source reference for a widget (typically a visualization or metric).

id.description: SF record id of the source asset (e.g. visualization id).

name.description: API name of the source asset.

textContent.description:
Optional content for type="text" widgets. The server converts this
plain text to the dashboard's Quill Delta representation, including
a trailing left-aligned newline. Ignored for non-text widget types.
Omit to create an empty text widget.

type.description:
Widget type. MUST be lowercase on write: "visualization",
"text", "filter", "image", "metric", "button", "container",
"extension", "summary", "parameter".

remove_widget_from_dashboard.name: remove_widget_from_dashboard
remove_widget_from_dashboard.description: Remove a widget and all its layout placements from a dashboard in one atomic operation. This tool handles the read-modify-write internally — you do NOT need to call get_dashboard or update_dashboard separately. Inputs: `dashboardIdOrApiName` (REQUIRED — the dashboard ID or API name), `widgetName` (REQUIRED — the name/key of the widget to remove, must match a key in the dashboard's widgets map). The tool removes the widget from the widgets map AND removes all placement entries referencing that widget from all layout pages. Returns: dashboardId, dashboardName, widgetName of the removed widget. Use when: removing a specific viz or widget from a dashboard. Do NOT use for deleting the entire dashboard (use delete_dashboard). To replace a widget, call remove_widget_from_dashboard then add_widget_to_dashboard.

dashboardIdOrApiName.description: The ID or API name of the target dashboard.

widgetName.description: The name/key of the widget to remove. Must match a key in the dashboard's widgets map.

add_global_filter_to_dashboard.name: add_global_filter_to_dashboard
add_global_filter_to_dashboard.description:
Add a global filter widget to a dashboard, backed by a Semantic Model field.
This tool handles constructing the full filter widget JSON and placing it on the
grid — you do NOT need to call get_dashboard or update_dashboard separately.

Inputs:
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (REQUIRED — the dashboard ID or API name)
- `semanticModelIdOrName` (REQUIRED — the SF record ID or API name of the
  Semantic Model containing the field to filter on)
- `objectName` (REQUIRED — the data object/table API name within the Semantic
  Model, e.g. "Account", "tc25_orders")
- `fieldName` (REQUIRED — the field API name to filter on, e.g. "Region",
  "Product_Category")
- `placement` (REQUIRED — object with `row`, `column`, `rowspan`, `colspan`
  for grid position, and optional `pageIndex` defaulting to 0)
- `dataType` (optional — Text, Number, Date, Boolean, measure; defaults to Text;
  case-sensitive)
- `selectionType` (optional — "single" or "multiple"; defaults to "multiple")
- `operator` (optional — filter comparison operator; use for pre-seeding a default
  selection. For relative date ranges supply `operator` alone: `CurrentQuarter`,
  `CurrentMonth`, `CurrentYear`, `PreviousMonth`, `PreviousQuarter`, `Yesterday`,
  `LastNDays`, etc. For value matching also supply `initialValues`: `Equals`,
  `In`, `Contains`, `GreaterThan`, etc.)
- `initialValues` (optional — default value(s) for the pre-selected state. Always
  pass as a JSON array, even for a single value (["West"] not "West"). Use a
  single-element array for exact-match operators, a multi-element array for In,
  or a numeric array for numeric comparisons. Omit for relative date operators.)

Examples:
  Add a Region filter pre-set to "West":
    operator: "Equals", initialValues: ["West"]
  Add a date filter defaulting to current quarter:
    operator: "CurrentQuarter"  (no initialValues needed)
  Add a multi-region filter pre-set to West + East:
    operator: "In", initialValues: ["West","East"]
- `filterLabel` (optional — display label; defaults to fieldName)
- `widgetName` (optional — unique name; auto-generated as "filter_N" if omitted)

Grid conventions: 48 columns, 20px row height, 1200px max width.
Common filter sizes: full-width = colspan 48 rowspan 4, half-width = colspan 24
rowspan 4.

Returns: dashboardId, dashboardName, widgetName of the added filter.

Use when: adding a global filter to a dashboard (e.g. "Add a Region filter",
"Create a date filter for Order Date").

Do NOT use for:
- Adding visualizations → use add_widget_to_dashboard
- Removing filters → use remove_widget_from_dashboard with the filter's widgetName
- Creating a dashboard from scratch → use create_dashboard

dashboardIdOrApiName.description: The ID or API name of the target dashboard.

dataType.description:
Data type of the field. Determines filter rendering.
Defaults to "Text" if omitted. Values are case-sensitive.

fieldName.description: The field API name within the data object to filter on (e.g. "Region", "Product_Category").

filterLabel.description: Optional display label for the filter widget. If omitted, defaults to the fieldName.

initialValues.description:
Optional. Default selected value(s) for the filter widget, used
together with `operator`. Always provide a JSON array, even for a
single value (["West"] not "West"). Use a single-element array for
exact-match operators (Equals: ["West"]), a multi-element array for
multi-value operators (In: ["West","East"]), or a numeric array for
numeric comparisons. Omit for relative date operators
(CurrentQuarter, etc.) where the operator alone determines the range.

objectName.description: The data object (table/view) API name within the Semantic Model (e.g. "Account", "tc25_orders").

operator.description:
Optional. Filter comparison operator for the default selection.
For relative date range operators (CurrentQuarter, CurrentMonth,
CurrentYear, CurrentFiscalQuarter, CurrentFiscalYear,
PreviousMonth, PreviousQuarter, Yesterday, LastNDays, etc.)
supply `operator` alone — no `initialValues` value is needed.
For value-matching operators (Equals, In, Values, Contains, etc.)
also supply `initialValues`.

placement.description: Grid placement for a widget on a dashboard page.

colspan.description: Width in grid columns (e.g. 24 for half-width, 48 for full-width).

pageIndex.description:
0-based index of the page within layouts[0].pages[]. Defaults
to 0 (first page). If the page does not exist, returns an error.

rowspan.description: Height in grid rows (e.g. 20 for a standard tile).

selectionType.description:
Whether the filter allows single or multiple selection.
Defaults to "multiple" if omitted.

semanticModelIdOrName.description: The SF record ID or API name of the Semantic Model that contains the field to filter on.

widgetName.description:
Optional unique widget name. If omitted, auto-generates as
"filter_<N>" where N avoids collisions with existing widgets.

add_dashboard_page.name: add_dashboard_page
add_dashboard_page.description:
Add a new page to a dashboard's layout. This tool handles the read-modify-write
internally -- you do NOT need to call get_dashboard or update_dashboard separately.

Inputs:
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (REQUIRED -- the dashboard ID or API name)
- `pageName` (internal API id for the page, e.g. "page_2"). Auto-derived
  as "page_N" (1-based) if omitted, but ALWAYS pass it explicitly so it
  matches what navigation widgets target -- keep the `page_1`, `page_2`,
  ... sequence contiguous.
- `pageLabel` (display label for the page, e.g. "Details"). ALWAYS set
  it -- an unset label renders a blank page tab. When the user gives no
  name, default to a meaningful label from the page's purpose, not a
  bare "Page N" placeholder.

Returns: dashboardId, dashboardName, pageName, pageIndex of the added page.

Use when: adding a new page to an existing dashboard (e.g. "Add a second page
called Details", "Create a new page for KPIs").

Do NOT use for:
- Creating a dashboard from scratch -> use create_dashboard
- Adding widgets to an existing page -> use add_widget_to_dashboard
- Removing a page -> use remove_dashboard_page

dashboardIdOrApiName.description: The ID or API name of the target dashboard.

pageLabel.description: Optional display label for the page (e.g. "Details").

pageName.description:
Internal name for the page (e.g. "page_2"). If omitted,
auto-generated as "page_N" where N is the new page index.

remove_dashboard_page.name: remove_dashboard_page
remove_dashboard_page.description:
Remove a page from a dashboard's layout by index. This tool handles the
read-modify-write internally -- you do NOT need to call get_dashboard or
update_dashboard separately. Widgets that only exist on the removed page are
also deleted from the dashboard's widget map.

Inputs:
- `dashboardIdOrApiName` (REQUIRED -- the dashboard ID or API name)
- `pageIndex` (REQUIRED -- 0-based index of the page to remove)

Returns: dashboardId, dashboardName, pageName, pageIndex of the removed page.

Use when: removing a page from an existing dashboard (e.g. "Remove the second
page", "Delete page 3").

Do NOT use for:
- Deleting the entire dashboard -> use delete_dashboard
- Removing a single widget from a page -> use remove_widget_from_dashboard
- Adding a page -> use add_dashboard_page

dashboardIdOrApiName.description: The ID or API name of the target dashboard.

pageIndex.description: 0-based index of the page to remove.
